# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 91
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 87 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, and four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`. Counting convention: a public definition is a
  non-private `def`, `abbrev`, `instance`, `structure` or `inductive` written
  in the source of the `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` and
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules; declarations generated by Lean
  (structure projections, constructors, recursors, matchers, `noConfusion`
  and the instance `MaskedTrigProducts.instDecidableEqTrig` produced by
  `deriving DecidableEq`) are not counted. The inventory is taken from the
  elaborated environment (509 public definitions: 418 with rows, 81 `def`
  and 6 `abbrev` quantities, and the four instances). Earlier versions of
  this page said 89 and 507: two definitions were left out of the running
  count, one when wave L2 was added and one when wave L5 was added.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is not formalized.
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The Index by label is a pointer table: each manuscript label (and one row
  for declarations with no direct label) points to the sections whose tables
  formalize it, each followed by the category phrase of that section's
  heading. It carries no per-declaration lists or qualifiers: what each
  declaration states and the analytic inputs it takes are stated once, in
  the section tables. Labelling convention: every backticked manuscript
  label in a section-table label cell is an assignment and creates an Index
  pointer; a label mentioned only as context goes in the "What it states"
  cell as "(Context: ...)"; a "no direct label" cell contains no manuscript
  label.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`,
  `PhaseContractions` and `L9Completed`) are whole results. Missing
  constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for
  example the noise `W` of `P:masked-quotient-obstruction`, the ground
  family of `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, the chain measures used for
  `L:uniform-series-tail`, the operator paths of `P:radius-mean-anchor`, the
  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`).
- The seventy-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules: 27 are whole-result
  modules (all with nothing supplied), 31 are narrower-result modules, and 18 are foundations or proof steps (`WaveKernel`,
  `SpectralHomog`, `TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `GaussianIBP`,
  `GaussianTest`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalFloor`, `SeriesType`,
  `H1Density`, `FiniteWick`, `GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`, `WaveGreen`,
  `WaveGreenFourier`, `SpaceTimePositivity`, `IntervalScalar`,
  `StaticPhaseCauchy`). Some modules without a section of their own are
  covered in the section of the module they serve. Together they model
  `H:homog` and give, by labelled result, 25 whole results (with the
  manuscript's hypotheses alone; none remains whole with named inputs), 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and steps or parts of
  30 further results
  (see `COMPLETION.md`), to the scopes specified below (the narrower
  conclusions are stated per result). Forty-seven (the 25 whole and 18
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and
  `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters`, `E:masked-time-schur` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`) need no supplied input:
  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also
  stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers
  `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the Rayleigh
  lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not
  formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under the
  full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` models
  clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses
  (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top
  of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (`GaussianIBP`).
  `L:variational-control-dilation` is stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its integral form
  and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum
  `E:variational-real-rayleigh` (over a weak-gradient `H^1(R^d)` built in
  `WeakSobolev`, since Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces); the identifications
  with `E W(Psi)^2` and `sqrt(-E_s)` are not formalized.
  `P:masked-spectral-growth` is stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_spectral_growth_paper`, and the
  homogeneity of the spectral measure, which the TeX derives in the proof of
  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, is derived from `H:homog`
  (`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Hence `P:clock-copy-obstruction` and the
  finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (with `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`)
  are stated with nothing supplied by the `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers. The
  rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (`N_0`, the scaling identities, the
  tails `E:damped-tail-norms`, and the upper bounds of
  `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`, for a measurable multiplier in `[0,1]` on
  the spectral measure and measurable Laplace domains `S subset S'`) is
  `DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper`, for an arbitrary family
  `G` with the mass identity `GreenMass G` as hypothesis, and is stated with
  `H:homog` alone (no `Gamma != 0`) and nothing supplied by
  `WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave`: `WaveGreen` builds the wave
  Green measures `G_s` for `d = 1, 2, 3` (in `d = 3` with Mathlib's
  `Measure.toSphere` taken as the surface measure, a definitional choice)
  and proves their mass `G_s(R^d) = s`, finiteness, support in the closed
  radius-`s` ball and the scaling `G_s(sA) = sG_1(A)`.
  `L:masked-time-completion` is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (`0
  < a < 1`, `T > 0`; no `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_time_completion_paper`: the
  completion `H_a` is built (`TimeCompletion`, Mathlib's completion of
  `L^2(0,T)` under the temporal form, over `C`), with positive
  semidefiniteness, separability, the continuous extension, the complexified
  norm identity, interval amplitudes, and density of the real compact smooth
  tests on `(0,T)`. `E:masked-time-schur` and `L:masked-temporal-modulation`
  are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by `time_schur_paper` and
  `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` for the defining double integral, and
  `E:masked-time-schur` also for the norm of `H_a` (`emb_norm_sq_le`).
  `L:masked-trig-products` and `L:masked-continuous-wave` are stated in this
  `H_a` with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied
  (`masked_trig_products_completed_paper`,
  `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper`). `P:frequency-row` and
  `C:frequency-time` are stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog`
  with `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`, and of `beta` for the corollary)
  by `frequency_row_paper` and `frequency_time_paper`, with the constant
  chosen before `d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h`. `L:occupation-kernel-row` and
  `L:spatial-physical-pair` are stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `D = q - 2a`) by `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
  and `spatial_physical_pair_paper`. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` is stated
  with the manuscript's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by
  `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper`; its clause for a real `H` after
  complexification is not formalized, and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier` is
  proved for any complex Banach space. `L:variational-heat-envelope` and the
  display of `L:variational-global-mean` are stated with the section's
  hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `variational_heat_envelope_paper` and `variational_global_mean_paper`; the
  latter's first sentence (all mixed derivatives bounded) is not formalized.
  `L:phase-bessel` is proved for any measure space and any complete complex
  inner product space and stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by
  `phase_bessel_paper` (separability carried and not used).
  `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` is stated with the proposition's
  hypotheses by `masked_quotient_obstruction_paper`, which also proves that
  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` satisfies `H:homog` (with `alpha = 1`) and
  `Gamma != 0`; `E W(F)^2` is read as the covariance functional of `E:cov`
  (the noise is not constructed, so this is a narrower result: the
  identification with noise variances is not formalized). The Rayleigh-form part of
  `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz
  bounds and `0 < I_Psi < infinity`, for the rate defined by
  `E:variational-real-rayleigh`) is stated with the section's hypotheses by
  `variational_unmasked_rate_paper`; its operator half (`H_s` self-adjoint,
  `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`) is not formalized. `L:spatial-static-controls` and
  `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` are stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper` and
  `spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper` (`SpatialOccupationCompleted`),
  with the score displays `E:spatial-static-score` and
  `E:spatial-smooth-score` in an existential form; their supremum forms take
  the named input `S1Bdd` there and are stated with nothing supplied in
  `L8Completed` (wave L8); `R_0` is positive and
  finite with nothing supplied, by the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <=
  2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2)` of `SpatialFourierBound`
  (`L:spatial-fourier-bound`, which the manuscript uses for the same purpose
  since `a284420`), so `R_0 < infinity` does not depend on `T:full-upper`. `L:positive-series-type` is stated with the
  lemma's hypotheses by `positive_series_type_paper`.
  `C:white-relative-width` and `L:white-clock-laplace` are stated with the
  section's hypotheses by `white_relative_width_paper` and
  `white_clock_laplace_paper`, the latter with the damping parameters
  `eta_1, eta_2 > 0` of `E:white-self-clock-transform` made explicit (the
  TeX gives them no sign). `L:inventory-product` is stated with the
  section's hypothesis `H:homog` by `inventory_product_paper`, with the
  explicit constant `inventoryConst alpha alpha0` fixed before `M` and `k`.
  `P:spatial-four-linear` and `P:spatial-energy-map` are stated with the
  section's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by the
  `_completed` wrappers of `SpatialOccupationL7Completed` (for example

  `spatial_energy_value_paper_completed`), which discharge the density of

  `P:occupation-physical-class` is stated with the section's hypotheses and
  the TeX's constants `R_sp` and `E_sp` by
  `occupation_physical_class_Esp_paper` (`SquarePairingBounds` discharged by

  In wave L8: `L:spatial-fourier-bound` is stated with the manuscript's
  constant `R_alpha` of `E:intro-spectral-mass` by
  `SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper`, through the

  `occupation_ceiling_sSup_K0_paper_completed`), and
  `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` with the section's hypotheses for `S_2^pos`

  `L:positive-raw-embedding` is stated with the section's hypotheses in
  narrower forms (the variance identity in integral form, the row bound and
  the scalar Schur bound) by
  `SpaceTimePositivity.positive_raw_variance_form_paper` and
  `OccupationCeilingFinite`. The integral identities of
  `L:occupation-raw-square` are proved for continuous compactly supported

  In wave L9: `L:low-alpha-convolution` is stated with `H:homog` and
  `alpha < 1` alone in `d = 1, 2, 3` by
  `L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed` (for the wave Green

  `P:raw-occupation-energy` is stated with the section's hypotheses and
  nothing supplied by `RawOccupationEnergy.raw_occupation_energy_paper`

  `E:raw-occupation-ratio`), over the class `O` modelled by joint measurable

  `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` is stated with the section's hypotheses and

  the lemma allows `m_i` modes in color `i` and the insertions

  Five further results are proved, with analytic inputs supplied as named
  hypotheses, for abstract objects whose identification with the
  manuscript's is not formalized, so they count among the narrower results:

  `M_R(Y_m)` and the residual noises not constructed; the moment bound of

  `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and `C:static-moment-constant-continuity` (for

  hypothesis structure `TypeContinuityInputs`: the coefficient series and

  `T:full-upper` at each temporal exponent and Cauchy-Schwarz),
  `L:raw-block-indexed-cone` (every conclusion for an abstract ground family
  of `S:compact-mean-family`, one hypothesis structure) and
  `L:uniform-series-tail` (the two facts of `L:terminal-wick` that its proof

  mixed moments, one hypothesis structure `TerminalWickInput`; `eps, delta

  parameters, in the hypothesis and in the conclusion; in wave L8
  `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` proves that structure for the
  chain integrals of a centered Gaussian field with nonnegative covariance,
  and `L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the
  two, with the chain measures fixed only by their total masses); their
  abstractions
  are explained in their sections. Parts of further results are formalized
  in wave L6, with named inputs where stated:
  `P:variational-positive-scores` (everything except `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`, the
  boundedness of the value sets and the supremum statements on the named

  `P:wave-two-variances` (the spectral core in full; the statement for
  `E|l_R|^2` with `E:variance-normalized-covariance`, the isometry `J` and

  comparison of `P:masked-noise-completion`, the facts about the wave Green

  summation to `E:interval-phase-bound`).
  Parts of three further results, and further steps of a fourth, are
  formalized in wave L8, with the inputs named in their sections:
  `P:variational-remove-mask` (`RemoveMask`: the masks and every rate
  statement with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for the
  Rayleigh-form rates; the point display `E:variational-unmasked-point-lower`
  from `E:raw-block-original-lower` of `P:raw-block-original-lower` as a
  supplied input, for a real function in place of the point moment),
  `L:terminal-wick` (`TerminalWick`, on the finite Wick formula of
  `FiniteWick`: every conclusion for real `r`, with the `L^2` strong
  measurability of the field products supplied and the chain measures entering
  only through their total masses `T^(2n)/(2n)!`, the measures `g_n^{T,x}` not
  being constructed; the comparison is stated for each mixed moment
  `E[Y_m Y_n]`, not for second moments of finite partial sums; and the Wick
  formula takes the joint measurability of the covariance on pairs of points,
  a restriction the manuscript does not make), `L:symplectic-free` (`SymplecticFree`: both
  compact-baseline displays on an abstract nonzero Hilbert space, with the
  free group, reversal and translations (`FreeWaveData`) and the convergence
  of the left Young sums supplied; the per-frequency symplectic identity and
  the force skewness for the `L^2` pairing), and the Cauchy and scalar steps
  of `P:static-phase-all-orders` (`StaticPhaseCauchy`: both displays for
  abstract Banach-space quantities, with the circle bound, entireness in the
  coupling, the coefficient identification, the norm comparisons, the cutoff
  removals and the free bound supplied).
  Parts of six further results are formalized in wave L9, with the inputs
  named in their sections: `L:fock-form` and `L:interval-contractions`
  (`FockForm`, on `GaussianHermite` and `HermiteFock`: `E:fock-sandwich` with
  the symmetry of the sandwiched operator, the band compression, the vacuum
  phase insertion and `E:interval-fock`, for finitely many multiplied
  Gaussian coordinates, from the spatial column bound and
  `E:interval-column` supplied as `FockColumn`), the multiplication bound
  `E:occupied-multiplication` of the proof of `P:mild-construction` (nothing
  supplied, for polynomials in finitely many standard Gaussians), and
  `L:complex-phase` and `L:interval-complex` (`ComplexPhaseScalar`: the
  numerical-range, scalar and Banach-algebra steps with nothing supplied;
  the operator bounds from Crouzeix-Palencia `E:cp-input` and the
  inverse-root integral representation as supplied inputs; the phase
  propagator itself is not constructed), and `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  (`HermiteWordFock`, nothing supplied, but only for one Gaussian mode per
  color and a single finite word; the multi-mode case and the sentence on
  finite sums and Bochner integrals of words are not formalized). Side
  conditions the TeX leaves
  implicit (a probability measure, integrability, measurability) are
  explicit hypotheses (one hypothesis is not implied by the TeX: the joint
  measurability of the covariance in `L:terminal-wick`, recorded there as an
  added restriction). Integrability is proved where a statement says so
  (as a conjunct or in a companion theorem); totalized integral identities
  (such as the continuous-`F` Gaussian bridge of `FiniteWick` and the
  `SymplecticFree` cancellation for arbitrary functions) and auxiliary
  bounds do not by themselves guarantee integrability, and extended
  nonnegative integrals (such as the physical pairing of
  `L:spatial-physical-pair`) need not be finite.
- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures (beyond finitely
  many independent standard Gaussians, `GaussianIBP`, the centered
  Gaussian laws `N(0,A)` on `R^m` of the finite comparison in
  `GaussianComparison`, and the finite Wick formula for centered Gaussian
  vectors and finitely many values of a centered Gaussian field in
  `FiniteWick`, and the normalized Hermite polynomials and the finite
  Gaussian Fock layer of `GaussianHermite` and `HermiteFock`), Fourier analysis (beyond the Gaussian transform of
  `P:masked-spectral-growth`, the auxiliary mask norm of
  `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, the wave-kernel and two-time Laplace
  transforms, the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in
  `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`, `WaveGreenFourier`), of
  Mathlib's sphere measure on `S^2` and Archimedes' law for it
  (`WaveGreenFourier`), the Gaussian spectral representation of `gamma_eps`
  and of the smoothed pairing (`LowAlphaConvolution`), the Gaussian Fourier
  pairing of `PhaseContractions`, the spectral identity of
  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`P:masked-quotient-obstruction`), the
  spectral form of the autocorrelation integral in
  `SpatialFourierBound`, `L:spatial-fourier-bound`, the spectral-mass
  identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` of `SpectralMassIdentity`, and the
  Gaussian Fourier multiplier of `DampedMultiplier`),
  infinite-dimensional spectral analysis and operator theory (beyond the
  finite-matrix results of `FiniteGaussianMatrix` and the abstract
  compact-operator facts of `SymplecticFree`) and limits in time or in a
  regularization of the equation or its solution are outside Lean; the
  scalar and norm-tail limits stated in their sections are formalized (for
  example the tails `E:damped-tail-norms` and `K_M(r) -> 0` as
  `M -> infinity` in `DampedNormsHomog`, the limit of the decay bound of
  `P:radius-mean-anchor` as `delta -> 0+`, and the abstract `L^2`
  regularization limit `u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` of `L:uniform-series-tail`
  in `UniformSeriesTail`, for an abstract family with the two facts of
  `L:terminal-wick`, which `TerminalWick` proves for nonnegative
  covariance). Where a Lean statement needs an
  analytic fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis
  of the theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
  yet public.
- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
  labeled statement of the revision cited above, or is a Lean-only
  auxiliary or example (such as a non-vacuity instance) with no
  counterpart in the manuscript. Such rows make no claim about the
  manuscript.

Declarations of the step modules live in `StratonovichHAMAudit.<Module>`
(file `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`); those of the library
modules in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.<Module>` (file
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean`). Status is assigned per
`claims.yaml` entry and need not coincide with this ledger's category
"auxiliary to the Lean proof route": helper lemmas have status
`internal` in `claims.yaml` (the four `PositiveGram` declarations and the
helpers of `TemporalEquilibrium`, `RadiusMeanAnchor`,
`MaskedTrigProducts`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalDilation`, `IndexedCone`,
`GaussianIBP`, `FiniteGaussianMatrix`,
`TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `ClockCopy`, `GaussianTest`,
`MaskedSpectralGrowth`, `TimeSchur`, `MaskedModulation`, `FrequencyRow`,
`OccupationKernelRow`, `TimeCompletion`, `MaskedContinuousWave`,
`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`, `DampedNormsHomog`, `VariationalMean`,
`PhaseBessel`, `WaveGreen`, `QuotientObstruction`, `GaussianComparison`,
`WaveTwoVariances`, `VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`,
`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`, `WhiteRelativeWidth`,
`WhiteClockLaplace`, `InventoryProduct`, `UniformSeriesTail`, `H1Density`,
`SpatialFourLinear`, `OccupationPhysicalClass`, `IntervalScalar`,
`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `SpectralMassIdentity`, `DampedMultiplier`,
`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`, `SpatialBracket`,
`RemoveMask`, `FiniteWick`, `TerminalWick`, `SymplecticFree`,
`StaticPhaseCauchy`, `L8Completed`, `WaveGreenFourier`,
`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, `RawOccupationEnergy`,
`OccupationCeilingExact`, `ComplexPhaseScalar`, `GaussianHermite`,
`HermiteFock` and `FockForm`); all others are `reusable` (`SeriesType`'s
`factorial_ge_exp` and `factorial_le_exp` are route auxiliaries kept
`reusable` as Stirling-type bounds, and some other route auxiliaries,
for example `VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn`,
`VariationalRate.rawCost_genuine`, `InventoryProduct.params`, the
mollifier facts `mollify`, `eLpNorm_mollify_le`, `tendsto_mollify`,
`grad_mollify` and `tendsto_bumpN_rOut` of `H1Density`,
`SpatialFourLinear.pairing_toReal_eq_C4` and `Nnorm_eq_sqrt`, and
`OccupationPhysicalClass.squareCS_of_sqrt` and `Tlin_unique`, are
`reusable` too).

## ActualEvent (proof steps)

Checks two scalar steps in the lower bound obtained from restarted time
blocks (Section `S:actual-raw-block-lower`). The first is the elementary
error-accumulation estimate for differences of ordered products, used in
the proof of `L:raw-block-restart`; the second is the normalization of the
linear Gaussian penalty in the proof of `P:raw-block-original-lower`.

| `P:raw-block-original-lower` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.ActualEvent.moderate_penalty` | For `delta > 0`, `delta (delta^(-1/4) / sqrt delta) = delta^(1/4)`. | The Gaussian change of law, the event on which the penalty bound holds, and the limit `delta -> 0`. |

## DimensionalMatrix (proof steps)

Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
(`L:masked-continuous-wave`; defined in Lean as `MaskedContinuousWave.bFn`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in
`L:symplectic-free`, which also defines the force `B(b)`.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.backward` | Definition: `[[cp, -sp/p], [p sp, cp]]`, the backward free matrix `S(-t)` at one frequency. | The interpretation of `cp, sp` as cosine and sine of a phase, and the continuous extension at zero frequency. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.coupling` | Definition: `[[0, 0], [H, 0]]`, the force `B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)` with `H` for `b`. | The meaning of `H` as a covariance coefficient. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward` | Definition: `[[cq, sq/q], [-q sq, cq]]`, the free matrix `S(t)` at one frequency. | As for `backward`. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.full_interaction` | For all real parameters (field division), `backward * coupling * forward = [[-(sp/p) H cq, -(sp/p) H (sq/q)], [cp H cq, cp H (sq/q)]]`, the unweighted product `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` at fixed frequencies. | The Bessel-weighted coordinate change and the weight `1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)` that turn it into `E:variance-normalized-kernel`; Fourier multiplication and covariance integrals; the zero-frequency case. |

## DirectEvent (proof steps)

`kappa_gt_one` checks the lower inequality `kappa > 1` of `E:kappa`
(`kappa = (4 - alpha - alpha_0)/(3 - alpha)` in `(1, 2)`); the proof of
`P:original-point-transfer` uses it in exactly this form ("since
`alpha < 2 < 3`, `a < 1`, we have `kappa > 1`"). The next three check the
exponent arithmetic of the exact scaling `delta = T^(-kappa)`,
`r_T = T delta` in `L:exact-canonical-scaling`, which does not itself use
`kappa > 1`.
The last three are 2x2 matrix identities for a scalar calibration from the
development of the manuscript; they are not stated in the revision cited
above.

|---|---|---|---|

| `L:exact-canonical-scaling` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DirectEvent.physical_scale` | For `T > 0` and `alpha < 3`, `T * T^(-kappa) = T^((a-1)/(3-alpha))`. | None. |
| `L:exact-canonical-scaling` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DirectEvent.noise_scale` | For `T > 0` and `alpha < 3`, `T^(-a/2) r_T^(2 - alpha/2) = sqrt delta`. | Scaling of the Gaussian noise and its covariance; equality in law of the rescaled solution. |
| `L:exact-canonical-scaling` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DirectEvent.vertex_scale` | For `T > 0` and `alpha < 3`, `T^(1 - a/2) r_T^(1 - alpha/2) = delta^(-1/2)`. | Scaling of the Green measure; extension to the full series and its second moment. |
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DirectEvent.gauge_inverse` | `gauge(-w) * gauge(w) = 1` for `gauge(w) = [[1,0],[w,1]]`. | None. |
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DirectEvent.gauge_drift` | `gauge(-w) * [[0,1],[1,0]] * gauge(w) = [[w,1],[1 - w^2, -w]]`. | The differential equation and its growth analysis. |

## HermiteWord (proof steps)

Checks the combinatorial core of `L:finite-word-cutoff` (exact cutoffs for
finite Gaussian words), which is applied in `P:static-phase-all-orders` and
`L:fixed-split`: if the initial vector has degree zero in every color, each
step raises a degree bound by one in its color and
the projection fixes every vector within the cutoff, inserting the
projection around each step does not change the word. The statements are
abstract (arbitrary types and maps). The companion file
`HermiteWordConsumer.lean` instantiates them with the scalar Hermite
recurrence `x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1)` as private worked examples; it
adds no public declarations. The Hermite/Fock realization is proved in
`FockForm` (`goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame`, `truncC_eq`, one
Gaussian coordinate per color) and applied in
`HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock` (next section).

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L:finite-word-cutoff` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.raw_support` | If the initial vector `v0` is Good at the zero count, each `J i` raises the degree bound by one in color `i` and each `F b` preserves it, then the uncut word output is Good at the color counts of the word. | None for the Fock model with one coordinate per color (`FockForm.goodDeg_insert`, applied in `HermiteWordFock`); colors with several coordinates are not formalized. |
| `L:finite-word-cutoff` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` | Under the same hypotheses (including the zero-count condition on `v0`), if `P` fixes every vector Good at a count at most `N` and the color counts of the word are at most `N`, then the cut and uncut words agree. | None for one coordinate per color (`FockForm.truncC_eq`); Bochner integrals of words are not formalized. |

## HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)

Applies `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` (the finite-word
induction of `L:finite-word-cutoff`, `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `a284420`, statement lines 2531-2553, display `E:finite-word-cutoff`
lines 2543-2550, proof lines 2555-2571) to the concrete Gaussian Fock model
of `FockForm`. `HermiteWord` predates the module system and is not a
`module`, so a `module` file cannot import it; this audit file is not a
`module` and imports both `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord` and
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FockForm`. In this one-mode special case
nothing is supplied: the four hypotheses of `cut_eq_raw` are
`FockForm.goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame` and `truncC_eq`.
The lemma itself is not formalized in full: with `m_i` modes in color `i` the
insertion is `J_i = sum_(j=1)^(m_i) M_(g_ij) (x) K_ij` (lines 2532-2538),
whereas Lean has `J_i = M_(g_i) (x) K_i`; this is a restriction of the
admissible operator data, not an omitted side condition.

Model (that of `FockForm` and `HermiteFock`). Coefficient vectors
`(Fin m -> N) -> X` over `m` colors with one standard Gaussian mode per
color (the TeX allows `m_i` modes in color `i`); the insertion of color `i`
is `J_i v = gmul i (K_i v)`, multiplication by `g_i` tensored with a
continuous linear operator `K_i` on `X`; the frames `F_b` act on `X` only;
the cutoff `P = truncC Nc` projects each color onto Hermite degree at most
`N_c`; the start vector is `vac u = 1 (x) u` (the TeX's
`(I (x) F_0)(1 (x) v)` with `u = F_0 v`). A word is a list of
(color, frame) pairs, read as in `HermiteWord` (`raw`, `cut`). The
statement is in normalized Hermite coefficients, where multiplication by
`g_i` is `a_i^* + a_i` (`HermiteFock.coord_smul_iota` identifies this with
multiplication of the Hermite expansion by the coordinate).

Narrower than the TeX: one mode per color; a single finite word (the
sentence on finite sums and Bochner integrals of words, lines 2551-2552, is
not formalized); `X` is a complex inner product space in `Type` (the
universe of `HermiteWord`), with no completeness used, which is more
general than the TeX's Hilbert space.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L:finite-word-cutoff` (`E:finite-word-cutoff` for the Fock model with one Gaussian mode per color; main TeX lines 2531-2553, proof 2555-2571) | `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock` | For colors `Fin m` with one standard Gaussian mode each, insertions `J_i = g_i (x) K_i` (`gmul i (K_i v)`, `K_i` continuous linear on a complex inner product space `X`), frames `T_b` acting on `X`, a start vector `u` (the TeX's `(I (x) F_0)(1 (x) v)` with `u = F_0 v`), per-color cutoffs `N_c` and a finite word `w` (a list of (color, frame) pairs) whose color counts are at most the cutoffs: the cut word, with `P = truncC Nc` before and after every insertion, equals the raw word. The lowering terms of `g_i` are retained. Proof: `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` with its four hypotheses discharged by `FockForm.goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame` and `truncC_eq`. Narrower than the TeX: `m_i = 1` mode per color; the statement is in normalized Hermite coefficients (multiplication by `g_i` is `a_i^* + a_i` there by `HermiteFock.coord_smul_iota`); `X` lives in `Type` and completeness is not used. | The colors with several modes `m_i > 1`, and the sentence on finite sums and Bochner integrals of words (lines 2551-2552); not formalized. |

## InteractionDriver (proof steps)

Checks parameter ranges, exponent bookkeeping and margins used in building
the operator-valued driver (Section `S:actual-operator-driver`). The ranges
and the Holder margin correspond to `E:driver-parameters`,
`L:driver-interval-limit` and `L:driver-holder-limit`; the Lean statements
make one explicit choice (the midpoint between `theta` and `H`) of the
exponent the manuscript only requires to lie in an interval. The
manuscript's `L:driver-holder-limit` lets that exponent be any point of the
interval; `holder_parameters` and `dyadic_ratio` check the midpoint
instance only. The Gaussian mixture and box statements belong to a
preliminary derivation; the Gaussian mixture rows are not stated in the
revision cited above. The box rows are the dimension-two case of a step of
`P:radius-mean-anchor`: its proof divides `Q(1-a) > 2d` by `2Q` to get
`e_anchor = (1-a)/2 - d/Q > 0` and combines `g_delta` with the radius
power. With `d = 2` and the Lean parameter `p` taken as the manuscript's
even moment exponent `Q` (not its averaging exponent `p`), `box_margin` is
that margin and `box_scale` that power bookkeeping. The general margin and
the proposition for abstract random paths are formalized in the section
`RadiusMeanAnchor` (a narrower result) below; these two rows remain as dimension-two instances.

## ClockCopy (whole result)

Formalizes `P:clock-copy-obstruction`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lines
7754-7904) in full, with its displays `E:cross-clock-lambda-weight`,
`E:clock-copy-obstruction` and `E:degree-one-clock-loss`, together with the
finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 803-919) and
`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. The module `ClockCopy` rests on four foundation
modules of the D4 layer (Fourier and Laplace analysis of the wave kernel
and the time kernel), whose rows are marked "[D4 foundation: <Module>]":
`WaveKernel` (`G_s hat` as `waveHat s xi = s sinc(s|xi|)`, which is
`sin(s|xi|)/|xi|` with value `s` at `0`; its bounds, scaling and Laplace
transform), `TimeFractional` (subordination
`r^(-a) = Gamma(a)^(-1) int l^(a-1) e^(-r l) dl`, the kernel `Psi_a` of
`E:averaged-clock-kernel` and its properties, and the two-time Laplace
lemma `int int e^(-as-bt-lam|s-t|) = (a+b+2lam)/((a+b)(a+lam)(b+lam))` for
complex `a, b` with positive real part), `SpectralHomog` (consequences of
the spectral homogeneity, `R_Gamma`, `h_Gamma`, and `Gamma != 0 => mu != 0`)
and `DampedNorms` (`N_1`, `N_2^2` of `E:damped-norm-definitions` and their
finiteness). `H:homog` is `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` with temporal
exponent `a = alpha0`; the wrappers `clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
`damped_norms_finite_paper` and `damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the results
with the manuscript's hypotheses (`Gamma != 0`, `theta > 0`,
`-1 <= rho <= 1` for the proposition; `Gamma != 0` is not assumed for the
lemma). These wrappers take ONE further input as an argument:
`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`, `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for Borel `A` and
`c > 0`, which the TeX derives from the scaling of `Gamma` and Fourier
uniqueness in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 851-852; the
same derivation is in the proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines
4718-4722). This input is now derived under `H:homog` by
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and
`ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper` and
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the three results with
nothing supplied (see "MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)"); the
statements of this section are unchanged. Its consequences
`mu{0} = 0`, `mu(B_r) = r^alpha mu(B_1)`, `int (1+|xi|^2)^(-1) dmu < inf`
(by the layer-cake formula), and the homogeneity of `R_Gamma` and `h_Gamma`
are proved; Lebesgue measure on `R^1` satisfies the input (see
`refutations/clock-copy/WrongDegreeOneConstant.lean`). Implicit hypotheses
made explicit: integrals over `(0,inf)` and `(0,inf)^2` are Bochner
integrals for Lebesgue measure (`TimeFractional.L0`, `TimeFractional.P2`).
Since the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, every integral
the paper asserts to be finite (`w_theta`, the `N_1` and `N_2` integrands,
the outer integrand of `N_2^2`, the `J` integrands and `2 theta/(2 theta +
l) w_theta`) comes with a proved integrability conclusion; the auxiliary
scaling identities `SpectralHomog.integral_comp_smul` (measurable `f` only)
and `ClockCopy.integral_rpow_div_add_scaling` (`c > 0` only, any `a`) are
identities of Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion,
and are used only where integrability is proved separately
(`ClockCopy.integrable_rpow_div_add` needs `0 < a < 1`). `G_s hat` is real,
so the complex conjugate in `N_2` is dropped. `Psi_a(theta|u-v|, .)` and
`|s-t|^(-a)` take Lean's junk values on the diagonal, a null set (the TeX
notes the diagonal is irrelevant). Hypotheses carried but unused: in
`clock_copy_obstruction_paper`, `rho >= -1` and the fields `dim`,
`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`
and the `Gamma` scaling of `HomogCovariance` (the latter replaced by the
supplied input); in `damped_norms_finite_paper`, the fields `dim`,
`Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`,
`mu_tempered`, `spectral`, the `Gamma` scaling and `alpha_range`; in
`damped_N2_nonneg_paper`, the fields `dim`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
`Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and
the `Gamma` scaling. The `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers use `mu_tempered`,
`spectral` and the `Gamma` scaling to derive the input. The proof route differs from the TeX, though the
statements do not. On the `K` side Lean does not smooth the covariance and
pass to a monotone limit: it expands `|s-t|^(-a)` by subordination and
applies Fubini on `(0,inf) x R^d x (0,inf)^2`, justified by an absolute
majorant built from `|G_s hat G_t hat| <= 2(1+s)(1+t)/(1+|xi|^2)`. This is
a different route, not the one after "Alternatively" in the TeX (lines
7824-7826), which bounds the density `w_theta` by homogeneity; Lean's
proof that `w_theta` is integrable (`weight_integrable`) does use bounds of
that shape, `C l^(a-1)` near zero (from `resolvent_sub_le`) and
`C l^(a-2)` at infinity, but derives them without homogeneity. The time
integral of the first display of the proof is the complex two-time lemma
at `theta -+ i|xi|`, and needs `mu{0} = 0`. On the `J` side the `(w,q)` substitution and the
resolvent identity are replaced by the real two-time lemma at
`c = (theta^2+|xi|^2)/2` and rate `theta l + l^2/2`, and `J_rho` is
dominated by `J_1` (the TeX's majorant through `Psi_a <= r^(-a)` and the
homogeneity of `h_Gamma` is not needed). For `alpha = 1` only the scaling
`int l^(a-1)/(c+l) dl = c^(a-1) int l^(a-1)/(1+l) dl` is used, not the
Beta value. Partial fractions and the strict inequality reuse
`StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter`. Not formalized in this section: `N_0`,
the scaling identities of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, the tails
`E:damped-tail-norms` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (all in
the section `DampedNormsHomog`, `N_0` with the mass identity
`G_s(R^d) = s` supplied), the identity
`Psi_a(r,v) = E (r+iZ)^(-a)`, the probabilistic interpretation of the
clocks and of `h_Gamma` as a heat average, and the remark
`R:clock-copy-scope`. The full wrapper hypotheses with `Gamma != 0` are
not instantiated in Lean (the audit examples use the zero witness of
`HomogCovariance`); the general theorems are instantiated at Lebesgue
measure on `R^1`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the
Lean proof route)"; the definitions `L0`, `P2`, `subKernel`, `psiKernel`,
`twoTimeC`, `twoTimeR`, `FK`, `MK` and `FJ` only name integrands and
measures and have no rows.

## ComplexPhaseScalar (narrower result: scalar steps of `L:complex-phase` and `L:interval-complex`; the weighted block map not identified with the propagator, the interval-norm telescoping not formalized; functional-calculus inputs supplied)

Wave L9 in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ComplexPhaseScalar.lean`. It
formalizes the scalar, numerical-range and Banach-algebra steps of
`L:complex-phase` (A complex phase bound; main TeX file
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, statement lines
2288-2310, proof 2312-2465) and of `L:interval-complex` (Complex sums and
changing phase weights; statement lines 2899-2917, proof 2919-2982), and
states both lemmas with their hypotheses in two layers. Class: inputs
supplied, conclusion weaker. Both lemmas are statements about the phase
propagator `M_z(h)` of `u'' + Lu = 0` on `X_lambda`; the propagator, its
identification with the weighted block matrix of functional-calculus
operators, and the operator functional calculus are not formalized. Proved
with nothing supplied: the constants (`1 - delta_a >= 3/4`,
`delta_a I_a <= pi/8`, `4 delta^2/(1-delta) <= 1/3`,
`1 + (1-delta)^(-1) <= 7/3`, the prefactor bound `<= 1/6`; lines 2355-2359,
2389-2393, 2424-2426; `I_a`, `delta_a` are `StaticPhaseCauchy.phaseI`,
`deltaA`); the scalar resolvent integral
`int_0^inf t^(-1/2) (lambda^2+t)^((a-3)/2) dt = lambda^(a-2) I_a` with
integrability and the operator-norm bound for any integrand dominated as at
lines 2349-2354 (`kappa_integral`, `resolvent_integral_le`, `q_sub_one_le`);
the Neumann bounds in any normed ring with summable geometric series
(for example a complete one) and `||1|| <= 1`
(`neumann_inverse_le`, `neumann_root_comparison`: `||Q - 1|| <= 1/6` gives
`||Q|| <= 7/6`, `Q` invertible, `||Q^(-1)|| <= 6/5`); the resolvent
difference as a ring identity (`resolvent_difference`) and the four-factor
norm product (`integrand_factor_le`); the form consequence of
`E:abstract-sandwich` for bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space, with
`A_rho^(-1/2)` the inverse of the continuous-functional-calculus square root
of `A_rho = rho^2 + A_0` (`form_of_sandwich`; invertibility proved for
`rho > 0`, so the sandwich hypothesis is not vacuous), and the adjoint
sandwich identity (`sandwich_adjoint_norm`); the numerical-range parabola
(lines 2373-2396, 2948-2958), with `s = 0` by `rho -> 0` (`form_opt_le`) and
`|Im r| <= lambda` for EVERY square root `r` of `w`; the scalar bounds of
lines 2398-2429 for `C_h`, `F_h`, `H_h` on the numerical range, with the
removable values at `w = 0` (`phaseG` is an `if` branch that supplies the
removable sine-quotient value, and `phaseH`, a product involving `phaseG`,
consequently has the correct value `0` there; divisions by `sqrt(w + lambda^2)` occur only where
`Re(w + lambda^2) > 0` is proved); the assembly constants and the bound of a
2x2 block operator on `H + H` by the sum of its block norms (lines
2430-2460); and the `L:interval-complex` instance of `E:interval-metric`
(lines 2966-2981): the multiplier form of the phase-weight change, the jump
ratio, and the product over jumps whose ending sets are pairwise disjoint.
The wrappers `complex_phase_range_paper` and `interval_complex_range_paper`
take exactly the lemmas' hypotheses (bounded `A_0 >= 0` self-adjoint
(`IsPositive`), `B` self-adjoint resp. `V` bounded, `0 < a < 1`, `d > 0`, the
sandwich bound, `lambda > 0`, the coupling condition, `h >= 0`) and conclude
`PhaseRangeBounds` at every point of `W(L)` (and, for
`L:interval-complex`, the adjoint sandwich bound), with nothing supplied.
The propagator wrappers `complex_phase_paper` and `interval_complex_paper`
add SUPPLIED inputs (named hypotheses, not formalized): Crouzeix-Palencia
`E:cp-input` (lines 2277-2286, imported in the TeX) for each of `C_h, F_h,
H_h` at `L` (operators `Cop, Fop, Hop` with `||Op|| <= (1+sqrt 2) M` whenever
the scalar function is bounded by `M` on `W(L)`; the holomorphy
precondition of lines 2405-2407 is discharged by the supplier), and the
inverse-root integral representation of lines 2329-2354 (resp. 2929-2944)
for `L^*` (an operator `Q'` with `Q' - 1 = pi^(-1) int_0^inf J(t) dt`, `J`
strongly measurable, `||J(t)|| <= (c/(1-delta_a)) t^(-1/2) kappa^(a-3)`,
`c = |z| d` resp. `D`; the bounded holomorphic calculus). They conclude the
three operator bounds `3, 6(1+lambda h), 6` (times `e^(lambda h)`),
`||Q' - 1|| <= 1/6`, `||Q'^*|| <= 7/6`, `||(Q'^(-1))^*|| <= 6/5`, and the bound
`100 e^(2 lambda h)` for the weighted block map built from these operators.
Narrower than the TeX: `E:complex-phase-bound` is concluded for that block
map, not for `M_z(h)` (the identification of lines 2433-2444, 2461-2464 and
2959-2962 is not formalized); the comparisons with `L` itself (`Q`,
`Q^(-1)`) are bounded by the same `neumann_root_comparison` but not named in
the wrappers; `s` is `sqrt(Re <A_0 u,u>)` (which equals `||A_0^(1/2) u||`,
not restated); `E:interval-metric` is the instance for given finite jump
data (`interval_metric_paper`; the weights' positivity is used only as
nonnegativity), and the general telescoping lemma for the interval metric
along a time partition (composition with the segment propagators) is not
proved (wave L10-FS0). The self-adjointness of `B` is carried but unused in
`complex_phase_range_paper` and `complex_phase_paper` (the hypothesis is
named `_hB`; the scalar route allows complex `<Bu,u>`). Mathlib's inner
product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, so the TeX's `<Tu,u>` is
`inner u (T u)`.

Controls (`refutations/complex-phase-scalar/`): (a) manuscript-claim
perturbations, each refuted at a witness satisfying the manuscript's other
hypotheses: `BlockExponent` (the scalar block-sum majorant
`(39+12x) e^x <= 100 e^x` in place of `100 e^(2x)`, `x = lambda h`; `x = 6`;
not an identified propagator bound), `NeumannInverse` (`norm(Q^(-1)) <= 1`
in place of `6/5`; `Q = 5/6`, a scalar multiple of the identity), `PhaseWeight`
(the loss factor unsquared in the multiplier, i.e. squared-norm, inequality,
where the TeX's unsquared factor is for norms; `rho_old = 2`, `rho_new = 1`, `x = 0`) and
`ParabolaQuarter` (the manuscript's `delta <= 1/4` dropped; `delta = 1/2`);
(c) a control of a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript's
domain: `ImaginaryRoot` refutes `abs(Im r) <= lambda/2` for the reduced-premise
implication of `im_root_le` (`r^2 = w`, `abs(w) <= Re w + 2 lambda^2`) at
`lambda = 1`, `w = -1`, which violates the numerical-range condition
`x >= -lambda^2/4` of main TeX line 2393; whether `lambda/2` fails under the
manuscript's full hypotheses is not decided. No control is of type (b), and
none relies on a junk value.

## DampedMultiplier (narrower result: `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, covariance-smoothing identification not formalized)

Formalizes the parts of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lemma lines
803-848, proof lines 850-919) that `DampedNormsHomog` left out: the lower
bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (display at lines 836-841; the
multiplier class and the Laplace domains at lines 826-834), and the smoothing
assertions at the end of the lemma (lines 845-847) and of its proof (lines
915-917). Read with `E:damped-norm-definitions` (lines 782-793) and
`G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)` (lines 777-778). `DampedNormsHomog`
and `WaveGreen` are unchanged; the extended wrappers are new declarations.
With this module and `DampedNormsHomog`, `WaveGreen`, every assertion of the
lemma except part of its closing smoothing sentence is a Lean conclusion under
`H:homog` with nothing supplied (`damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave`). The
smoothing sentence is formalized in the narrower reading fixed by Le's
decision 2 for wave L8 (below): spatial smoothing of the covariance only as
the membership of `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)` in the multiplier class (the spectral
identification of `p_eps * Gamma` is not stated), and Gaussian smoothing of
the Green kernel as the multiplier on the transforms of `G_s` in every `d`,
identified with `N_{2,m,S}` in `d = 1` by `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`
and, since wave L9, in `d = 1, 2, 3` by
`WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave` (`full_wave` itself
does not contain that identification). The spectral identification of the
smoothed covariance remains unformalized.

Formalized.
- The lower bounds: `0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta)` (`N1on_nonneg`, for any measure
  and `a > 0`) and `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` (`N2onSq_nonneg`, for an s-finite
  measure with `int (1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1) dmu < infinity`, `mu{0} = 0`,
  `0 < a < 1`, `theta > 0`, measurable `S`); `damped_multiplier_comparison`
  states the whole display, both bounds with the integrability of the
  integrands, for a general measure (the upper bounds are
  `DampedNormsHomog.N1on_smoothed_mono` and `N2onSq_smoothed_mono`).
- The multiplier class `IsMultiplier` (measurable, values in `[0,1]`; the
  TeX's `m : R^d -> [0,1]` measurable, lines 826-827), closed under products
  (`IsMultiplier.mul`), containing the Gaussian multipliers
  `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)`, `eta >= 0` (`gaussMult`, `isMultiplier_gaussMult`).
- The `N_0` mass sentence (lines 846-847, proof lines 916-917): convolution
  with a probability measure preserves `GreenMass` (`greenMass_conv`), so
  `N_0` is unchanged and equals `theta^(-2)` (`N0_conv`); instantiated with the
  Gaussian `gaussKernel v` and the wave Green measures, `d = 1, 2, 3`
  (`gauss_waveGreen_mass`).
- Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (lines 845-846, proof lines
  915-916): for a finite `G`, the characteristic function of `p * G`
  (`p = gaussKernel v`, `v >= 0`) is `e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2) G hat`
  (`charFun_gaussKernel_conv`), so the product of the transforms is multiplied
  by `e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` (`charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv`). Hence the second
  norm of `p * G` (`N2GreenSq`: `E:damped-norm-definitions` with kernel `K_S`
  and `G_s hat` the characteristic function of `G_s`) equals the second norm
  of `G` with spectral measure `e^(-v norm(xi)^2) mu(dxi)` (`N2GreenSq_gauss`,
  every `d`, `G_s` finite for `s > 0`). Under the Fourier identity
  `GreenFourier G` (`G_s hat = waveHat s`, lines 777-778) the second norm of
  `G` is `N2onSq` (`N2GreenSq_eq`) and that of `p * G` is
  `N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` with `m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` (`N2GreenSq_gauss_eq`);
  the Fourier identity is proved in `d = 1` (`greenFourier_one`, from
  `WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`) and, in wave L9, in `d = 1, 2, 3`
  (`WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier`).

Wrappers. `damped_homogeneous_norms_full_paper`: under `H:homog`
(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal exponent `a = alpha0`,
no `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX) and `GreenMass G` (the input of
`DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper`, line 881), the conclusions
of that wrapper with its item on `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` extended to
both bounds, plus the Gaussian multipliers and products, and, for every
`v >= 0`, `GreenMass` and `N_0` of `p * G` and `N2GreenSq_gauss`.
`damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave`: the same with `G := waveGreen d` and
`H:homog` only (`GreenMass` by `WaveGreen.waveGreen_greenMass` with the field
`dim`). `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper`: under `H:homog` and
`GreenFourier G`, for `v >= 0`, `theta > 0`, measurable `S subset S'`: the
outer integrands of the second norms of `G` and of `p * G` and of
`N2onSq(m mu, S)`, `N2onSq(mu, S')` are integrable; the second norm of `G` is
`N2onSq alpha0 theta S mu`; that of `p * G` is `N2onSq alpha0 theta S (m mu)`
with `m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2)`; and `0 <= N2onSq(m mu, S) <= N2onSq(mu, S')`.
`damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`: the same in `d = 1` with
`G := waveGreen 1` and nothing supplied.

Inputs. `GreenMass G` (line 881) as in `DampedNormsHomog`, a hypothesis on
the parameter `G`, discharged for the wave Green measures.
`GreenFourier G` is used only for the identification of the second norm of
`G` (and of `p * G`) with `N2onSq`: `G_s` finite and its characteristic
function equal to `waveHat s` for `s > 0`, i.e. that the `G_s hat` of lines
777-778 is the Fourier transform of `G_s`, which the TeX uses when it pairs
`G_theta(s,x)` with `G_theta(t,y)` (lines 794-797). It is no stronger than that
identity. Proved for `d = 1` (`greenFourier_one`) and, in wave L9, for
`d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier`), where `fourier_paper` is
instantiated as `WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`. The
lemma's own `N_1`, `N_2` are defined through `waveHat`
(`DampedNorms`), so no conclusion of `full_wave` depends on it.

Readings and narrower forms (Le's decision 2 for wave L8).
- "Spatial Gaussian smoothing ... give[s] multipliers in this class" (line
  845) is formalized as the membership of `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)` in the class;
  the spectral identity that the spectral measure of `p_eps * Gamma` is
  `e^(-c eps norm(xi)^2) mu` is not stated (it needs Fubini against the
  locally finite, infinite `Gamma`).
- "Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel give[s] multipliers in this class"
  is formalized as `N2GreenSq_gauss` in every `d` (transforms of measures), and
  as an identity of `N2onSq` norms in every `d = 1, 2, 3`
  (`damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one` and, wave L9,
  `WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`).
- The source's Gaussian `p_eta` (pp. 13-14 of the source; main lines 1674 and
  4698) is represented by the centered Gaussian `gaussKernel v = N(0, v I)`,
  the image of Mathlib's `stdGaussian` under `x -> sqrt(v) x`; every
  normalization `p_eta = N(0, c eta I)` is `gaussKernel (c eta)`. The TeX does
  not fix `c` in this lemma.
- Commentary only, not formalized: "the scaling identities above are asserted
  for the original covariance only" (lines 843-844) and "It is used after time
  integration, not pointwise" (lines 911-912).

Conventions and junk values. `N2GreenSq` is a complex Bochner integral (the
TeX's `int G_s hat conj(G_t hat) dmu` is complex before time integration); a
non-integrable integrand would give the value `0`. `N2GreenSq_gauss` and
`N2GreenSq_eq` are equalities of integrals whose integrands agree almost
everywhere on `(0,inf)^2` (`N2GreenOuter_gauss_ae`, `N2GreenOuter_ae_eq`), so
they hold whether or not the integrands are integrable; `fourier_paper` and
`fourier_one` conclude the integrability of all four outer integrands.
`gaussKernel v` with `v < 0` is the Dirac mass at `0` (`sqrt v = 0`); every
statement where that matters carries `v >= 0` (`gauss_waveGreen_mass` holds for
every `v`). `N_0` uses `(G s univ).toReal`, which is `s` under `GreenMass`.

Hypotheses of `H:homog` used. Directly: `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
`mu_radon` (s-finiteness of `mu`) and, in `full_wave`, `dim`; the other fields
used are those used by the called lemmas
(`DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper`,
`DampedNormsHomog.homog_spectral_facts`,
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper`). No field is claimed unused here.

Proof route. The lower bounds follow the TeX: the nonnegative integrand for
`N_1` (line 913); for `N_2`, the representation
`N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 = int_S w_theta^(m mu)` of `DampedNormsHomog.N2onSq_eq`
with `w_theta >= 0`, where the TeX uses `B_theta(lambda,xi) >= 0` by positive
definiteness (lines 900-911). The smoothing assertions have no TeX proof beyond
lines 915-917; the Lean route is Mathlib's convolution and
characteristic-function calculus (`Measure.conv`, `charFun_conv`,
`charFun_map_smul`, `charFun_stdGaussian`). Route-only helpers are "no direct
label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Refutations (`refutations/damped-multiplier/`), all without junk-value
reliance: `GaussianSign` (`e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)` in the class for every real
`eta`; false at `eta = -1`, `norm(xi) = 1`), `SumNotClosed` (the class closed
under sums; `1 + 1 = 2 > 1`), `MassNonProbability` (mass preserved by
convolution with any finite measure; `rho = 2 delta_0`, `G_s = s delta_0`),
`FourierExponent` (`e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` instead of `e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2)` for
one smoothed transform; `G = delta_0`, `v = 1`).

## DampedNormsHomog (narrower result: `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` without the general multiplier lower bounds, which are in `DampedMultiplier`; covariance-smoothing identification not formalized)

Formalizes the rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`: definitions
`E:damped-norm-definitions`, lines 782-792; lemma, lines 803-848, with the
tails `E:damped-tail-norms` at lines 822-825 and the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` with its definitions at lines 826-847, display
at lines 836-841; proof, lines 849-919, the comparison at lines 894-917). The finiteness part and
`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0` were already formalized (`DampedNorms`, `ClockCopy`,
re-issued with nothing supplied in `ClockCopyHomog`). This module adds
`N_0(theta) = theta^(-2)`, the scaling identities
`N_1(theta) = theta^(alpha+alpha0-2) N_1(1)` and
`N_2(theta)^2 = theta^(-beta) N_2(1)^2` with `beta = 4-alpha-alpha0`, both
tails `N_1^(M)(1) -> 0` and `N_2^(M)(1) -> 0` of `E:damped-tail-norms`
(also `N_2^(M)(1)^2 -> 0` and the tail form `N_2^(M)(1)^2 >= 0`), and the
upper bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. The wrapper
`damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` bundles all of these with the finiteness
part and `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. It assumes `H:homog`
(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal
exponent `a = alpha0`) and NOT `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX, plus one
input, `GreenMass G`, used only by the `N_0` conclusions (discharged by
`WaveGreen`).

Input of this module: `GreenMass G`, the mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` for `s > 0`
that the proof uses at line 881 (the TeX imports it from the source, Chen
(2.5)). This module defines no wave Green measure, so `N0 G theta` is
defined for an arbitrary family `G` of measures on `R^d` and `GreenMass G`
is exactly the identity the TeX uses, no stronger. All other conclusions of
the wrapper hold under `H:homog` alone (they do not use `GreenMass`). The
input is discharged in wave L6 by the module `WaveGreen` (section below):
`WaveGreen.waveGreen_greenMass` proves `GreenMass (waveGreen d)` for
`d = 1, 2, 3`, and `WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave` states the
lemma with nothing supplied, except the general multiplier lower bounds
`0 <= N_{1,m,S}`, `0 <= N_{2,m,S}^2` and the closing smoothing remark (both
are in `DampedMultiplier`, the remark in its narrower reading).

The multiplier comparison `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (lines 826-847,
display 836-841; at `975feb3` this was a one-sentence smoothing and
truncation claim, which wave L5 read, by Le's decision, as a multiplier and a
Laplace-domain restriction; the manuscript at `a284420` states that reading
itself). The lemma takes a measurable `m : R^d -> [0,1]` and measurable
`S subset S' subset (0,inf)`, defines `N_{1,m,S}(theta)` (replace `mu` by
`m mu` and restrict the `lambda` integral of `N_1` to `S`) and
`N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` (replace `mu` by `m mu` and the temporal kernel by
`K_S(r) = Gamma_E(alpha0)^(-1) int_S e^(-lambda abs(r)) lambda^(alpha0-1) dlambda`),
and asserts, for every `theta > 0`, `0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta) <=
N_{1,1,S'}(theta)` and `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 <= N_{2,1,S'}(theta)^2`,
for full and tail domains, with the scaling identities asserted only for the
original covariance. In Lean: `m` is `g : R^d -> [0,inf)`, measurable with
`g <= 1`, and `m mu` is `smoothed mu g`; `N_{1,m,S}` is
`N1on a theta S (smoothed mu g)`, `K_S` is `KS a S`, and `N_{2,m,S}^2` is
`N2onSq a theta S (smoothed mu g)`, with all `lambda`-integrals over
`S cap (0,inf)` for any measurable `S subset S'` in `R` (this contains the
TeX's `S subset S' subset (0,inf)`). Proved (`N1on_smoothed_mono`,
`N2onSq_smoothed_mono`, item 4 of the wrapper): both upper bounds, with the
integrands integrable; `S' = (0,inf)` gives the full norms (`N1on_univ`,
`N2onSq_univ`) and `S' = (M,inf)`, `theta = 1` the tails, the TeX's choices
at line 914. The lower bounds `0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta)` and `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` for
a general `m` and `S` and the whole display with both bounds are proved in
`DampedMultiplier` (wave L8: `N1on_nonneg`, `N2onSq_nonneg`,
`damped_multiplier_comparison`), and the closing remarks on Gaussian spatial
and Green smoothing in a narrower form (`isMultiplier_gaussMult`: membership
of the Gaussian multiplier only, without the spectral identification of the
smoothed covariance; `greenMass_conv`, `N0_conv`: the `N_0` mass identity;
`N2GreenSq_gauss`: Green smoothing on the transforms of `G_s`, identified with
`N_{2,m,S}` in `d = 1` by `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one` and in
`d = 1, 2, 3` by `WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`);
this module proves the upper bounds. The TeX applies the comparison at lines 1145-1155 (the
Laplace domains `A_e`, Green smoothing) and 1664-1673 (the Gaussian
multipliers "can be removed in the upper bounds").

Abstractions: `N1tail a M mu` and `K_M` (`KM`) integrate `lambda` over
`(M,inf) cap (0,inf)`, which is the TeX's `int_M^inf` for `M >= 0`; only
`M -> inf` is asserted. `N2tail` is `sqrt(N2tailSq)`, the printed form of
`E:damped-tail-norms`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values:
- Every integral the lemma asserts finite comes with an integrability
  conclusion (the `N_0` integrand, the tail integrands, the integrands of
  the smoothed and restricted norms), since a Lean Bochner integral of a
  non-integrable function is `0`. `N1_scaling` alone is an identity of Lean
  integrals; integrability is `DampedNorms.N1_integrable`.
- `K_S(0)` is a divergent integral for `S = (M,inf)`, and its Lean value is
  `0`. This happens only on the diagonal `s = t`, a `P2`-null set, so no
  statement depends on it; `integral_FKS_eq` holds at every `(s,t)` because
  both sides use the same totalized integral.
- `N2tail = sqrt(N2tailSq)` is not a junk square root under `H:homog`:
  `N2tailSq >= 0` is proved (`N2tail_props`). `N0` uses
  `(G s univ).toReal`, which equals `s` under `GreenMass` (no infinite-mass
  junk).
- The general lemmas state their side conditions: s-finiteness of `mu`,
  `mu`-integrability of `(1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1)`, `mu{0} = 0`, measurability of
  `g` and of `S`, `S'`, and `0 < a < 1`, `theta > 0`.

Hypotheses of `H:homog` used by the wrapper: `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
`threshold`, `alpha_range` (for `alpha > 0`), `mu_radon`, and, through
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, `mu_tempered`,
`spectral` and `scaling`. The fields `dim`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
`Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef` and `mu_even` are carried but unused.

Proof route (differs from the TeX in the first two items, same statements):
- `N_2` scaling: instead of changing `(s,t,xi)` in the spectral formula, both
  sides are written as `int_0^inf w_theta` (`ClockCopy.K_eq_integral_weight`)
  and the one-dimensional substitution `lambda = theta u` is combined with
  `w_theta(theta u) = theta^(a+alpha-5) w_1(u)` (`weight_scaling`). `N_1`
  scaling uses the same substitution and `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)`.
- Tails and truncation: instead of dominated convergence in `(s,t,xi)`, the
  subordinated integrand `DampedNorms.FK` is restricted to `lambda in S`
  (`FKS`) and Fubini gives `N_S(theta)^2 = int_(S cap (0,inf)) w_theta`
  (`N2onSq_eq`). The tail limit is the tail of the integrable `w_1`, and
  nonnegativity is `w_theta >= 0` (the TeX uses positive definiteness of the
  tail kernel). The facts `0 <= K_M <= |r|^(-alpha0)` and `K_M(r) -> 0` for
  `r != 0` used by the TeX are proved (`KS_nonneg`, `KS_le`, `KM_tendsto`)
  but are not needed by this route.
- Multiplier comparison: the same order as the TeX (lines 894-913). For each
  `lambda` the time integral comes first and is nonnegative for every `xi`;
  then `N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 = int_S w_theta^(m mu)` (`N2onSq_eq`) and the
  weights are compared at each `lambda` (`weight_smoothed_le`). The TeX gets
  `B_theta(lambda,xi) >= 0` from positive definiteness of
  `e^(-lambda abs(s-t))`; here the time integral is evaluated in closed form, so
  `w_theta(lambda)` is a `mu`-integral of an explicit nonnegative function of
  `xi`. For `N_1`, `R_(g mu) <= R_mu` (`resolvent_smoothed_le`), as at lines
  912-913.

Narrower conclusions: of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`, this module
proves the upper bounds; the lower bounds and the narrower forms of the
smoothing remarks (see the `DampedMultiplier` section) are in
`DampedMultiplier`; `N_0` is
proved here for any family `G` satisfying `GreenMass G`; for the wave Green
measures it is `WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen`, with nothing supplied. The tails
are stated at `theta = 1`, as in the TeX; the restricted norms are stated
for every `theta > 0`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to
the Lean proof route)"; the definition `FKS` only names the restricted
subordinated integrand and has no row.

## DriverParameters (whole result)

Formalizes the claim after `E:driver-parameters` that its strict intervals
are nonempty, under the parameter part of `H:homog` with `a = alpha_0`
(`notes/integrated_actual_operator_driver.tex`, which retains `H:homog`).
These theorems assume only the numerical part of `H:homog` (a
generalization); `HomogHypothesis.parameters_nonempty_paper` restates the
result under the full hypothesis. Only `0 < a < 1` and `a + alpha < 2` are used.

## FiniteGaussianMatrix (whole result)

Formalizes the finite-dimensional part of Section `S:compact-gaussian`
(`notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex` at `a284420`): Lemma
`L:gaussian-trace-bounds` (lines 47-90), Proposition
`P:finite-gaussian-matrix` (lines 98-177, including the Hermitian core
`E:finite-hermitian-gaussian`, line 150, and the Hermitian dilation, lines
156-169) and Remark `R:gaussian-one-variance-test` (lines 179-193). It uses
two modules: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/GaussianIBP.lean`, a reusable
foundation for finite Gaussian integration by parts, and
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FiniteGaussianMatrix.lean`, which contains the
three results. `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is reused from
`GaussianScalarPowers` (finite Hoelder, the integer-power bound, and
`E Z^r <= (E Z)^r` in the bootstrap). The three results are
stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by the wrappers
`gaussian_trace_bounds_paper`, `finite_hermitian_gaussian_paper`,
`finite_gaussian_matrix_paper` and `gaussian_one_variance_test_paper`.
Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The integration by parts
`E[g_k P(g)] = E[d_k P(g)]` and the integrability of polynomial moments
(TeX lines 122-126) are proved, not assumed.

Abstractions and why they are faithful.
- **Gaussians.** "Independent real standard Gaussians" are `g : Fin N -> Omega -> R`
  on an arbitrary probability space with `iIndepFun g P` and
  `HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P` for every `k`.
  `GaussianIBP.map_eq_stdPi` shows that their joint law is
  `stdPi N = Measure.pi (fun _ => gaussianReal 0 1)`. The general theorems are
  stated on `stdPi N` and transferred to the probability space through
  `integral_comp_eq_stdPi`.
- **One-dimensional integration by parts** comes from Mathlib's whole-line
  integration by parts and the density identity `phi' = -x phi`.
- **`N`-dimensional integration by parts** uses Fubini along `Fin.insertNth k`.
  The partial derivative is a hypothesis on every coordinate slice.
- **Matrices** are complex matrices indexed by finite types.
- **`||A||_{S_p}^p = Tr((A^*A)^m)`** for `p = 2m` is `schattenPow A m`, the
  real part of that trace. `schattenPow_trace` proves that the trace is real
  and nonnegative, so taking the real part loses nothing.
  `||A||_{S_p} = schattenNorm A m = (schattenPow A m)^(1/(2m))`.
- **`|Y|` and `V^(1/2)`** are `CFC.abs Y` and `CFC.sqrt V`, the continuous
  functional calculus under `MatrixOrder`. `abs_pow_even` and
  `schattenNorm_sqrt` give the identities the TeX uses:
  `|Y|^(2j) = Y^(2j)` and `||V^(1/2)||_{S_p}^p = Tr V^m`.
- **Real traces.** The TeX compares several traces as real numbers. Lean
  compares their real parts. `gaussian_trace_bounds_paper` also records
  that the imaginary parts of its right-hand traces vanish; the other
  wrappers state real-part bounds only, and the reality of those traces
  follows from the proved matrix lemmas (`trace_psd`, `trace_mul_pow_im`).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
- the measurability of the Gaussians (inside `HasLaw`);
- the integrability of `||X||_{S_p}^p` and of `Tr Y^(2m)`, which is part of
  each conclusion because the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function
  is `0` in Lean;
- the evenness of `p`, stated as `p = 2m` with `m >= 1` a natural number.

Every real power has a nonnegative base, so no statement holds through a
junk value.

Hypotheses carried but unused: `o, n, N >= 1` in
`finite_gaussian_matrix_paper` (`[Nonempty o] [Nonempty n] (_hN : 1 <= N)`).
The general theorem `finite_gaussian_matrix_zero` also covers the empty
family `N = 0`.

Proof route. The statements are the manuscript's; four steps differ from the
TeX route:
- The doubly stochastic step diagonalizes `D' = U^* D U` and applies Jensen's
  inequality to `t^m` (`convexOn_pow`) instead of the tangent-line
  inequality.
- The derivative of `t -> Re Tr(B (Y + t B_k)^j)` is computed in the type
  synonym `NMat n`, matrices with the L-infinity operator norm. This avoids
  the product-topology diamond on `Matrix`. Polynomial growth is bounded with
  the same norm.
- The integration by parts is applied to real parts of traces, which are
  real-valued functions.
- The `m = 1` case of `E:finite-hermitian-gaussian` follows from the same
  integration-by-parts identity with an empty word, where the TeX invokes
  independence directly.

Not formalized: the infinite-dimensional part of `S:compact-gaussian`,
namely `L:cutoff-factorization`, `P:cutoff-singular-values`,
`P:compact-two-envelopes`, `L:compact-positive-order`,
`P:localized-finite-variance`, `C:finite-gaussian-operators` and
`P:cutoff-boundary-tests`. These need Schatten classes and singular values of
compact operators on Hilbert space, Courant-Fischer, and Sobolev spaces on
the torus.
