## SpatialFourierBound (whole result)

Formalizes `L:spatial-fourier-bound` (Deterministic Fourier bound for the
spatial energy, `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`,
statement lines 101-111 with the display `E:spatial-fourier-bound` at lines
106-109, proof lines 113-164; it is new at `a284420`, introduced at lines
98-99). The quantities are `A_sp(g) = B_Gamma(g^2,g^2)` and
`b(g) = norm(grad g)_2^2` of line 35, with `B_Gamma` of
`E:spatial-physical-pair` (lines 12-17). The module proves, for every real
unit `g` in `C_c^inf(R^d)` and every covariance allowed by `H:homog`
(including `Gamma = 0` and singular covariances; no `Gamma != 0` is assumed,
as in the lemma), `b(g) > 0` and

  `0 <= A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2)`,

with `R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2)` (`SpectralHomog.resolvent mu 1`;
main TeX lines 7714-7723 at `a284420`). The lemma writes the constant as
`R_alpha` of `E:intro-spectral-mass` (main TeX line 531,
`R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`) and uses
`R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha` (lines 149-155, from the resolvent
calculation in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`); the identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (and `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha`) is proved in `SpectralMassIdentity` (`resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`, `resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper`, wave L8), and `SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper` states the lemma with the constant `R_alpha`; this module keeps the constant `R_Gamma(1)`. The manuscript now proves "`R_0` is finite" of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (lines 166-170) by this lemma (proof lines 185-188),
not by the finiteness of `S_1^pos`; the consequence for `R_0` itself is drawn
in `SpatialSmoothRatio` (`R0_pos_finite`, `spatial_smooth_ratio_R0_paper`),
so `R_0 < inf` does not depend on `T:full-upper`, in the manuscript and in
Lean.

Labelling. `spatial_fourier_bound_paper` is `L:spatial-fourier-bound` with the lemma's hypotheses (constant `R_Gamma(1)`; the lemma as printed, with `R_alpha`, is `SpectralMassIdentity.spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper`); `spatial_fourier_bound` is the
general form of the display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`; the proof steps that
have a sentence in the TeX proof are labelled as those steps;
`gradEnergy_pos` is the statement's `b > 0` (line 105; proof lines 114-115;
the proof of `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` states it again at lines 180-182).

Definitions: `autocorr` (`c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx`; the package's one
autocorrelation, for which `VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos` is stated), `spatialPair`
(`B_Gamma(F,G)` as the iterated Bochner integral of real functions; the TeX's
form is the `[0,inf]`-valued `OccupationKernelRow.pairing`; the
identification of the two is not proved in this module, and is proved for
continuous, compactly supported, nonnegative functions and locally finite
`Gamma` by `SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair`),
`spatialEnergy` (`A_sp`), `gradEnergy` (`b`, through the operator norm of the
Frechet derivative, which equals the Euclidean norm of the gradient),
`fourierQ` (`Q hat(xi) = int Q(x) e^(i <xi,x>) dx`, the convention of
`HomogHypothesis.IsSpectralMeasure`), `IsUnitTest` (smooth, compact support,
`int g^2 = 1`: the profiles of lines 103-104 and 168). `fourierQ` uses
`e^(+i <xi,x>)`, the exponent of `E:masked-spectral-convention`; the TeX
proof's unnormalized transform `F_0 Q(xi) = int e^(-i xi.x) Q(x) dx` (lines
116-118) is its complex conjugate for real `Q`, so `norm(fourierQ Q) =
abs(F_0 Q)` and every statement here, which uses only the modulus, is the
TeX's.

Proof route (the TeX proof, lines 113-164, follows the same route; helpers
without a TeX sentence are "auxiliary to the Lean proof route"):
`c_Q = Q * Q(-.)` is smooth with compact support, hence a Schwartz function
(`HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap`), so the spectral convention applies to it;
a hand Fubini gives `int c_Q(x) e^(i <xi,x>) dx = norm(Q hat(xi))^2`, so
`A_sp(g) = int norm(Q hat)^2 dmu` with `Q = g^2`; `norm(Q hat) <= norm(Q)_1 = 1`
and, by integration by parts with values in `C`,
`norm(xi) norm(Q hat(xi)) <= 2 sqrt(b)`; hence
`norm(Q hat)^2 <= 8b/(4b + norm(xi)^2)`, and
`int mu(dxi)/(4b+norm(xi)^2) = R_Gamma(2 sqrt b) = (2 sqrt b)^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)`
(`SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog`; the homogeneity of `mu` from
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). `b(g) > 0`
(`gradEnergy_pos`, `d >= 1`): `b = 0` forces `grad g = 0`, so `g` is constant
and, having compact support in the noncompact `R^d`, zero, as in the proof of
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 114-115); the proof of `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`
(lines 180-182) argues instead by the Fourier support of a function with zero
weak gradient (same conclusion). The claim is false for `d = 0`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the integrability of `c_Q` against `Gamma`
(`A_sp < inf`), of `norm(Q hat)^2` and of `1/(1+norm(xi)^2)` against `mu` are
conclusions (a Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`).
`integral_autocorr_eq_spectral` and `norm_fourierQ_le` alone are statements
about Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion. Hypotheses
of `H:homog` used by `spatial_fourier_bound_paper`: `dim` (`d >= 1`),
`alpha0_pos` and `threshold` (`alpha < 2`), `Gamma_radon`, `mu_radon`,
`spectral`, and `mu_tempered` and `scaling` (through
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Carried but unused: `alpha0_lt_one`,
`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `alpha_range`.
Supplied inputs: none. Not proved in this module: the identification of
`spatialPair` with `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (proved for continuous,
compactly supported, nonnegative profiles and locally finite `Gamma` by
`SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair`). The bound is for `C_c^inf` profiles; its extension to `H^1` is
`P:spatial-four-linear`, formalized in `SpatialFourLinear` through `R_0`
(not through this module's deterministic bound), with the density of
`H1Density` (completed in `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`).

Refutations (`refutations/spatial-fourier-bound/`): `ScalarExponent`
(`2^alpha` instead of `2^(1+alpha)` in `scalar_identity`, at `alpha = b = 1`),
`FourierNormHalf` (`norm(Q hat) <= norm(Q)_1/2`, at `xi = 0` for `Q = g^2`),
`ConstantFactor` (the bound with `2^(alpha-1)`, with `Gamma` Lebesgue,
`mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`, where `A_sp(g) = 1`; outside `H:homog`, inside the
general theorem's hypotheses). No junk-value reliance.

## SpatialFourLinear (narrower result: `P:spatial-four-linear` with sequential continuity; rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes two propositions of the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`):
`P:spatial-four-linear` (statement lines 219-237, proof 239-298) with the
displays `E:spatial-homogeneous-bound` (line 224), `E:spatial-square-CS`
(lines 225-227) and `E:spatial-four-linear` (lines 231-234), and
`P:spatial-energy-map` (statement lines 300-325, proof 327-348) with
`E:spatial-energy-map` (lines 309-314) and `E:spatial-static-energy-score`
(lines 316-322), in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpatialFourLinear.lean` (wave
L7-d). The `_paper` wrappers take the section's standing assumptions (lines
4-10: `H:homog` as `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, so `a = alpha0`,
and `Gamma != 0`) and one named input, `hdense`, which is discharged in
`SpatialOccupationL7Completed` (section below).

Objects reused, not redefined: `B_Gamma` is the extended pairing
`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` of `L:spatial-physical-pair` (a lower integral
in `[0,inf]`), so `A_sp(f) = B_Gamma(f^2, f^2)` and `B_Gamma(f^2, h^2)` are
`pairing Gamma (zE f^2) (zE h^2)`; on smooth profiles it agrees with the real
`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair` (`SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair`).
`R_0` is `SpatialSmoothRatio.R0`, unit profiles are
`SpatialStaticControls.IsUnitH1`, and `H^1` is the weak-gradient space of
`WeakSobolev`. A real `H^1` profile is an `H^1` pair `(f, g)` (`IsH1Pair`:
`f, g` in `L^2`, `g` a weak gradient of `f`), so that `N(f)` (`Nnorm alpha f
g`, line 221) and `b(f) = int ||g||^2` are written with the named gradient;
the weak gradient is a.e. unique (`WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique`), so
this is faithful. New definitions: `l2`, `Nnorm`, `IsH1Pair`, `H1Tendsto`
(`H^1` convergence of profiles, that is `L^2` convergence of each function
and its weak gradient), `C4` (line 229, a Bochner
integral against `nu = pairMeasure Gamma`), `ratioSetH1` and `Rsp` (`R_sp`,
line 235), `energySet` and `Esp` (`E_sp`, lines 302-306), `energyValue` (the
right side of `E:spatial-energy-map`), `F0` (`F_0`, lines 319-321), and the
route predicate `SquareBound` (the conclusion of the Fatou step).

Named input, discharged in `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`: `hdense`, the
density of test functions in `H^1` (every `f` in `L^2` with an `L^2` weak
gradient `g` is the `L^2` limit of test functions `phi_n` with
`VariationalFloor.grad (phi_n) -> g` in `L^2`). It stands for the proof
sentence at lines 262-268 ("Smooth compact functions are dense in `H^1`", by
cutoff and mollification) and is no stronger; the separability remark there is
not used. Its body is verbatim `H1Density.H1TestDense d` (wave L7-c), which
`H1Density.h1TestDense d` proves, so the input is discharged at integration in
the completion module `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`. Every `_paper` wrapper
uses `hdense` except `spatial_Asp_pos_paper` (positivity needs no density).
The `sSup` form `spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_paper` also takes the named
input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` (the boundedness claim of
`P:variational-positive-scores`), as in `SpatialOccupationCompleted`; it is
proved in wave L8 and discharged in `L8Completed`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `H^1` profiles carry their gradient;
finiteness is part of each `[0,inf]` bound (an `ofReal` right side); real
values of pairings (`toReal`) are taken only where finiteness is proved;
`R_sp` and `E_sp` are `Real.sSup`s whose nonemptiness and boundedness are
proved in the same wrappers. Clauses of `H:homog` used (per the module doc
comment): `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`, `alpha_range`, `threshold`
(for `d >= 1`, `0 < alpha < 2`, `M_a > 0`), `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`
(symmetry of `B_Gamma`), `spectral` (positivity of smooth signed
covariance), `mu_radon`, `mu_tempered` and `scaling` (through
`SpatialSmoothRatio`: `R_0` in `(0,inf)`, positivity, smooth dilation);
positivity of `A_sp` (`spatial_Asp_pos_paper`) uses only `Gamma_radon` and
`scaling`. `Gamma_tempered` is not used by the extension, continuity,
`R_sp = R_0` and energy-value statements, but the two energy-score wrappers
(`spatial_static_energy_score_paper` and its `sSup` form) use it: they apply
`SpatialOccupationCompleted.spatial_smooth_score_completed_paper` (and its
`sSup` form), whose discharge of `StaticControls` calls
`SpatialStaticControls.spatial_static_score_paper`, which uses
`hH.Gamma_tempered`. Carried but unused by every wrapper: `Gamma_posdef`,
`mu_even`.

Proof route, as in the TeX unless stated: the smooth homogeneous bound by
normalization in `R_0` (`smooth_homog_bound`); positive semidefiniteness of
`B_Gamma` on smooth signed profiles from the spectral identity and the
covariance Cauchy-Schwarz (`spatialPair_self_nonneg`, `spatialPair_sq_le`);
the Fatou step along a.e.-convergent subsequences of the density
approximants (`squareBound_of_smooth`; Lean extracts the subsequences for
`f` and `h` separately); Cauchy-Schwarz under `nu` for
`E:spatial-four-linear`; telescoping for continuity. Differences:
`E:spatial-square-CS` on `H^1` passes the smooth inequality
`B(phi^2,psi^2)^2 <= A_sp(phi) A_sp(psi)` to the limit by continuity of `C_4`
(the TeX passes positive semidefiniteness to combinations of `H^1` squares);
`b > 0` on unit profiles (lines 288-289) uses
`VariationalFloor.ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero` (mollification), not
the Fourier support argument; positivity of `A_sp` (lines 291-296) uses a
compact set of positive measure and Mathlib's continuity of the measure of
its translates, not `L^2` translation continuity of `1_E`, and assumes only
a.e.-strong measurability and `f` not a.e. zero (no `H^1` membership); for
`E:spatial-energy-map` the upper bound applies `E:spatial-homogeneous-bound`
and weighted AM-GM (`young_bound`) to every unit `H^1` profile and the lower
bound dilates smooth unit tests only (`energyValue_mem`), so the extension of
`E:spatial-dilation` to `H^1` (lines 328-330) is not formalized and not
needed; the scores follow from `E:spatial-smooth-score`
(`SpatialSmoothRatio`) by the substitution `score_identity` and continuity of
the scalar maps along smooth ratios increasing to `R_0`.

Narrower than the TeX: joint continuity of `C_4` on `(H^1)^4` is stated
sequentially (`H1Tendsto` of each of the four pairs), which is continuity for
the `H^1` seminorm topology but is not a `Continuous` statement; continuity of
`A_sp` and of the square pairings (proof, lines 282-283) is not restated (they
are `C4 f f f f` and `C4 f f h h` as real values, `pairing_toReal_eq_C4`);
`E:spatial-static-energy-score` is proved in the existential form (every `y`
below `M_a^(-1/k) F_0(E_sp)` is exceeded by some `I_Psi - v_Psi/2`, with the
package's real-Rayleigh rate and integral-form cost), and in the `sSup` form
only on `S1Bdd`. `spatial_four_linear_paper` bundles every claim of the
proposition except multilinearity and `|C_4| <= R_0 prod N(f_j)`, which are in
`spatial_four_linear_multilinear_paper` and `spatial_four_linear_bound_paper`.
Not formalized: the separability of `H^1` (lines 266-268), the TeX's common
a.e. subsequence (Lean uses one per profile), the `H^1` dilation. Junk values:
`l2 f = 0` off `L^2`; `C4` is `0` for a non-integrable integrand (every `C4`
statement is under `SquareBound` or for test functions, where it is
integrable, except the symmetries `C4_comm_*` and `pairing_toReal_eq_C4`,
which also holds when the pairing is `top`, both sides then being `0`); `Rsp`,
`Esp` are `0` for an empty or unbounded set (the wrappers prove nonempty and
bounded above); `ratioSetH1` divides by `(int ||g||^2)^(alpha/2)`, positive on
unit pairs (`gradL2_pos`); `spatialPair_self_nonneg` is a Bochner statement
that asserts no integrability. `squarePairingBounds_paper` restates
`E:spatial-homogeneous-bound` and the squared `[0,inf]` form of
`E:spatial-square-CS` in the spelling of
`OccupationPhysicalClass.SquarePairingBounds`;
`SpatialOccupationL7Completed.squarePairingBounds_holds` uses it to discharge
that input.

Refutations (`refutations/spatial-four-linear/`): `EnergyConstant` (half the
constant in `young_bound`, at `alpha = R = beta = 1`), `EnergyExponent`
(exponent `1` on `R` in `young_bound`, at `alpha = 1, R = 4, beta = 16`),
`Maximizer` (the maximizer `beta = alpha R` in `energy_attain`, at
`alpha = 1, R = 4`), `ZeroCovariance` (`pairing_sq_pos` without
`Gamma != 0`, with `Gamma = 0` on `R^1` and `f = 1`). No junk-value reliance.

## SpatialOccupationCompleted (narrower results: Rayleigh-form rate and integral-form cost, their identification not formalized)

Integration module of wave L6 for Section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
of `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (at `a284420`), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpatialOccupationCompleted.lean`. It discharges
the two named inputs of the wave's spatial modules under the section's
standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a nonzero covariance satisfying `H:homog`,
`a = alpha0`) and re-issues the manuscript wrappers without them:

- `rayleighFloor_of_homog`: `SpatialStaticControls.RayleighFloor Gamma`
  (for every nonnegative nonzero test function `z`, the Rayleigh set of
  `U_z = Gamma * z` contains a positive value), from the dilation floor
  `VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor` at `V = U_z` (with `alpha < 2` from
  `H:homog`, and the integrability and bound of `U_z` from
  `SpatialStaticControls.convZ_props`). This positivity route differs from
  the TeX's (lines 57-62, through `P:variational-unmasked-rate` and
  `P:compact-original-common-trial`).
- `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper`: `L:spatial-static-controls`,
  part (i) (lines 40-49), with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses.
- `staticControls_of_homog`: `SpatialSmoothRatio.StaticControls alpha0 Gamma`
  from `SpatialStaticControls.spatial_static_score_paper` (part (ii),
  existential form), with the Rayleigh set of `x -> 1 * U_z(x)` rewritten as
  that of `U_z`, and `B_Gamma(z,z).toReal = SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair
  Gamma z z` (`SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair`).
- `spatial_smooth_score_completed_paper`,
  `spatial_smooth_score_sSup_completed_paper`,
  `R0_finite_of_S1Bdd_completed_paper`,
  `spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper`: the four `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`
  wrappers (lines 166-176) without `StaticControls`. The supremum forms keep
  the named input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` exactly where the
  originals had it (proved in wave L8; `L8Completed` re-issues the `sSup`
  forms with nothing supplied).

Nothing else is supplied. The boundaries of the instantiated results (the
Rayleigh-form rate and the integral-form cost of `VariationalDilation`, whose
identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` is outside Lean; the
existential form of `E:spatial-static-score` and `E:spatial-smooth-score`)
are those recorded in the `SpatialStaticControls`, `SpatialSmoothRatio` and
`VariationalRate` sections. The refutations `FloorNeedsNonzero` and
`R0NeedsNonzero` show that `Gamma != 0` cannot be dropped (the zero
covariance satisfies `H:homog`).

## SpatialOccupationL7Completed (narrower results: class `O` bridge and rate and cost identification not formalized; joint continuity only in sequential form)

Integration module of wave L7 for Section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation` of
`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (at `a284420`), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpatialOccupationL7Completed.lean`. It discharges
two cross-item inputs under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a
nonzero covariance satisfying `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`) and re-issues the
manuscript wrappers without them. It defines no new object.

1. The density input `hdense` of `SpatialFourLinear`. It stands for the
   sentence "Smooth compact functions are dense in `H^1`" of the proof of
   `P:spatial-four-linear` (lines 262-268), and its type is the body of
   `H1Density.H1TestDense d`, which `H1Density.h1TestDense d` (wave L7-c)
   proves for every `d`. Re-issued without `hdense` (name `<source>_completed`,
   each proof one line): the general theorems `squareBound_of_smooth` (the
   Fatou step, lines 270-275), `C4_square_CS` and `square_pairing_CS`
   (`E:spatial-square-CS` on `H^1`), and the `_paper` wrappers
   `spatial_homogeneous_bound_paper`, `spatial_square_CS_paper`,
   `spatial_four_linear_bound_paper`, `spatial_four_linear_multilinear_paper`,
   `spatial_four_linear_continuous_paper`, `spatial_ratio_H1_paper`,
   `spatial_four_linear_paper` (`P:spatial-four-linear`, lines 219-237),
   `squarePairingBounds_paper`, `spatial_energy_value_paper`
   (`E:spatial-energy-map`, lines 309-314), `spatial_static_energy_score_paper`
   and `spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_paper` (`E:spatial-static-energy-score`,
   lines 316-322). `SpatialFourLinear.spatial_Asp_pos_paper` takes no density
   input and is not re-issued; the auxiliary `SpatialFourLinear.squareBound_R0`
   (no label) is not re-issued either. `H1Density` gives `L^2` convergence of
   the functions and gradients only; the a.e.-convergent subsequence of lines
   270-271 is extracted inside `SpatialFourLinear.squareBound_of_smooth`, so
   nothing else is supplied.
2. The input `OccupationPhysicalClass.SquarePairingBounds Gamma alpha R_0` of
   `P:occupation-physical-class` (two conclusions of `P:spatial-four-linear`:
   `E:spatial-homogeneous-bound` and `E:spatial-square-CS` in the squared
   `[0,inf]` form). `squarePairingBounds_holds` proves it under `H:homog` and
   `Gamma != 0` (from `squarePairingBounds_paper_completed`), and
   `occupation_physical_class_completed_paper` is
   `OccupationPhysicalClass.occupation_physical_class_paper` without it.
   `occupation_physical_class_Esp_paper` restates `E:occupation-physical-bound`
   and `E:occupation-own-energy` (lines 395-397, 399-403) in the TeX's own
   constants: `J(g) <= R_star R_sp T(g)^(alpha/2)` and `E_star^O <=
   R_star^(2/(2-alpha)) E_sp` with `R_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Rsp Gamma alpha` and
   `E_sp = SpatialFourLinear.Esp Gamma`, using `R_sp = R_0` and
   `E:spatial-energy-map` (`spatial_energy_value_paper_completed`;
   `OccupationPhysicalClass.spEnergyVal` and `SpatialFourLinear.energyValue`
   have the same body). So the source module's reading of `R_sp` as `R_0` and
   of `E_sp` as the formula `spEnergyVal alpha R_0` is no longer a narrowing.

The wrappers take exactly the section's standing assumptions
(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, `Gamma != 0`; for

left in one theorem: `spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_paper_completed` keeps

g_s(x)`), the construction of such representatives from strong

## SpatialSmoothRatio (narrower result: `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`, rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (The finite smooth spatial ratio,
`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`, lines 166-217) with its
displays `E:spatial-smooth-score` (lines 171-176) and `E:spatial-dilation`
(lines 189-195), under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: a
nonzero covariance satisfying `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`), written
`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and `Gamma != 0`.

What is proved:
- First claim, input-free (`spatial_smooth_ratio_R0_paper`): for every real
  unit `g` in `C_c^inf(R^d)`, `b(g) > 0`, `A_sp(g)` is a genuine integral and
  positive, `0 < R(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1)`; the ratio set is nonempty and
  bounded above, `0 < R_0 <= 2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1)` and `R(g) <= R_0`, i.e.
  `R_0` is a positive finite real number. Finiteness is by the route of the
  TeX (lines 185-188): the deterministic bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
  (`SpatialFourierBound`, constant `R_Gamma(1)`), not the finiteness of
  `S_1^pos`. So `R_0 < inf` does not depend on `T:full-upper`, for every
  `Gamma` in `H:homog` including singular ones. (Before `a284420` the
  manuscript bounded every ratio by the finite `S_1^pos`.)
  Positivity as in the TeX (lines 182-187), from `Gamma(B_r) > 0` and
  positivity of the autocorrelation of `g^2 >= 0` near `0` (lines 88-91;
  imported as `VariationalFloor.measure_ball_pos` and
  `VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos`), plus a normalized bump
  (`exists_unitTest`).
- `E:spatial-dilation` on `C_c^inf` (`spatial_dilation_paper`).
- `E:spatial-smooth-score` in the EXISTENTIAL form of Le's decision 2
  (`spatial_smooth_score_paper`): for every unit `g` and every `y` below
  `k [R(g) alpha^(alpha/2)/(8 M_a q^(q/2))]^(1/k)` (`k = 3-alpha`, `q = 4-alpha`,
  `M_a = TemporalEquilibrium.mass alpha0`) some `Psi in C_pos` has
  `y < I_Psi - v_Psi/2`. This form is implied by the TeX's
  `S_1^pos >= ...` and equivalent to it whenever `S_1^pos` is finite; it needs
  no `S1Bdd`. On the named input `S1Bdd` the TeX's `sSup` form
  (`spatial_smooth_score_sSup_paper`) is also proved, and so is the bound
  `R_0 <= 8 M_a q^(q/2) (S_1^pos/k)^k / alpha^(alpha/2)`
  (`R0_finite_of_S1Bdd_paper`), `E:spatial-smooth-score` solved for `R(g)`:
  the manuscript's route to finiteness before `a284420`, which now keeps
  `S_1^pos` only for the score inequality (lines 213-215). `spatial_smooth_ratio_paper`
  states both claims together.

Supplied inputs (named hypotheses):
- `StaticControls a Gamma` = `L:spatial-static-controls` (lines 40-96; wave
  item L6-f; discharged from `SpatialStaticControls` in
  `SpatialOccupationCompleted`):
  for every nonnegative nonzero test `z`, the Rayleigh set of `Gamma * z` is
  bounded above (part of "positive and finite", lines 47-48) and
  `E:spatial-static-score` (lines 50-53) holds in the existential form, with
  `lambda_z(1) = rayleighRate (Gamma * z)` and
  `B_Gamma(z,z) = spatialPair Gamma z z`. It is that lemma's conclusion (the
  TeX's form with a finite `S_1^pos` implies it), so no stronger than the
  manuscript. Used only by the score statements.
- `VariationalRate.S1Bdd a Gamma` (`BddAbove score1Set`, the first claim of
  `P:variational-positive-scores`, unmasked TeX lines 270-274, whose manuscript
  proof uses `T:full-upper`; Le's decision 1): only for the `sSup` form and
  "`S1Bdd` implies `R_0` finite" (the manuscript at `a284420` also retains
  the finite real `S_1^pos` only for the score inequality, lines 213-215).
  `S1Bdd` is proved in wave L8 (`L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed`), and
  `L8Completed` re-issues the `sSup` wrappers without it.
The L6-d foundations are imported, not assumed: `Gamma(B_r) > 0`
(`VariationalFloor.measure_ball_pos`), positivity of `B_Gamma(Q,Q)` for
nonnegative nonzero continuous compactly supported `Q`
(`VariationalFloor.autocorr_pos`, stated for
`SpatialFourierBound.autocorr`, the package's one autocorrelation), and the
weak gradient of a test function (`VariationalFloor.grad`,
`VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test`). The coefficient-one score set,
`S1Bdd` and `S1pos` are `VariationalRate.score1Set`, `VariationalRate.S1Bdd`,
`VariationalRate.S1pos`, and `M_a > 0` is `TemporalEquilibrium.mass_pos`.
`StaticControls` is discharged in `SpatialOccupationCompleted` (outside this
section).

Abstractions and why faithful: `I_Psi`, `v_Psi`, `C_pos` are those of
`VariationalDilation` (rate by the real Rayleigh form, cost in integral form;
their identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` is outside Lean,
`P:variational-unmasked-rate`, `L:compact-raw-profile`); `B_Gamma` is the real
iterated integral `SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair`; `U_l g = l^(d/2) g(l .)`
is `WeakSobolev.dilL2`; `lambda_z(1)^2` is the supremum of
`WeakSobolev.rayleighSet (Gamma * z)`. `R0` and `VariationalRate.S1pos` are `sSup`s; every
statement about `R0` establishes nonemptiness and boundedness of `ratioSet`
(the positivity statements assert both; `R0_finite_of_S1Bdd` and its
`_paper` wrapper assert boundedness, and their proofs establish nonemptiness
by `exists_unitTest`),
and `S1pos` is used
only under `S1Bdd`, so no statement rests on the `sSup` junk value; `ratio`
uses Lean division, but `b(g) > 0` on unit tests in `d >= 1`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `d >= 1`, `0 < alpha < 2` and
`M_alpha0 > 0` are derived from `H:homog` (`homog_consequences`; the general
forms state them). The pairing identity `int (Gamma * G) F = B_Gamma(F,G)`
used at lines 198-199 is proved with integrability (`integral_conv_mul`), and
`Gamma * z` is continuous (`conv_continuous`). Hypotheses of `H:homog` used:
`dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`, `alpha_range`, `threshold`,
`Gamma_radon`, `mu_radon`, `spectral`, `mu_tempered`, `scaling`. Carried but
unused: `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`; in
`spatial_dilation_paper` also `Gamma != 0`.

Proof-route differences: `b(g) > 0` by constancy, as in the proof of
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 114-115), not by Fourier support as in this
proof (lines 180-182); the optimisation (lines
200-213) substitutes the maximiser `L = q X^(1/k)` directly instead of
maximising `L - C L^q` (`score_algebra`).

Narrower conclusions: `E:spatial-smooth-score` is proved in the existential
form; its `sSup` form, and the bound on `R_0` by `S_1^pos`, rest on `S1Bdd`
(proved in wave L8, `L8Completed`);
`B_Gamma` is the real iterated integral. Not proved inside
`SpatialSmoothRatio`: the identification of `spatialPair` with
`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (it is proved, on the continuous, compactly
supported, nonnegative profiles used here and locally finite `Gamma`, by
`SpatialStaticControls.pairing_eq_spatialPair` and used in `SpatialOccupationCompleted`);
`L:spatial-static-controls` itself (it is in `SpatialStaticControls`,
supplied here as `StaticControls`).
Fallback (`R0Fin` as a named input) not used.

Refutations (`refutations/spatial-smooth-ratio/`): `ScoreConstant` (the factor
`2` dropped in `score_algebra`, at `alpha = M = R = 1`), `DilationExponent`
(`A_sp(U_l g) = l^(alpha+1) A_sp(g)`, with Lebesgue `Gamma`, `alpha = 0`,
`l = 2`), `GradDilation` (`b(U_l g) = l b(g)`, at `l = 2`),
`DropGammaNonzero` (`0 < R_0` without `Gamma != 0`: for `Gamma = mu = 0`,
`R_0 = sup {0} = 0`). No junk-value reliance.

## SpatialStaticControls (narrower result: `L:spatial-static-controls`, rate and cost identification not formalized)

Formalizes `L:spatial-static-controls` (Smooth temporal controls) of the
section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`): statement lines
40-54 (the definition of `lambda_z(c)^2`, lines 42-46; the display
`E:spatial-static-score`, lines 50-53), proof lines 56-96. The section's
standing assumptions (lines 4-10) are a nonzero covariance from `H:homog`
and `a = alpha0`; `U_z = Gamma * z` pointwise for smooth compact `z` (lines
37-38). The wrappers carry `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
`Gamma != 0`, and use the exponent `alpha0`.

Objects. `lamSq U c` is `sSup` of the real Rayleigh set
(`WeakSobolev.rayleighSet`) of the potential `c U`, that is the supremum of
`c int U g^2 - ||grad g||_2^2` over unit `g` in `H^1(R^d;R)` (weak
gradients); `lam U c = sqrt (lamSq U c)` and `lamZ Gamma z = lam (Gamma * z)`
is `lambda_z`. The definition is the TeX's display with a general potential;
for the bounded potentials used here the side condition of
`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic (`isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded`),
so the set is the manuscript's set. `I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are the package's
`VariationalDilation.integratedRate` (the integral of the real-Rayleigh rate)
and `VariationalDilation.rawCost` (the integral form of the cost); their
identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`,
`L:compact-raw-profile`) stays outside Lean, as for `VariationalDilation`.
`B_Gamma(z,z)` is `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (the extended nonnegative
integral of `E:spatial-physical-pair`) at `zE z = ofReal o z`;
`pairing_bridge` proves it finite and equal to `ofReal (int z U_z)`, and the
statements use its `toReal` only after that. `M_a` is
`TemporalEquilibrium.mass` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`) and `f_a` is
`TemporalEquilibrium.density`.

Part (i). `spatial_static_controls_rate_paper` proves, for a nonnegative
nonzero test function `z`: every `y -> z(x-y)` is `Gamma`-integrable; for
`c > 0` the Rayleigh set of `c U_z` is nonempty and bounded above (so
`lambda_z(c)^2` is a finite supremum), `0 < lambda_z(c)^2`, `0 < lambda_z(c)`;
and `lambda_z` is Lipschitz on every `[c_1, c_2]` with `c_1 > 0`. The general
form `static_rate` also gives `|lambda_z(c)^2 - lambda_z(c')^2| <= M |c - c'|`
for every upper bound `M` of `U_z` (the TeX's constant `||U_z||_inf`, lines
62-63) without any floor. Positivity rests on the named input
`RayleighFloor Gamma`: for every nonnegative nonzero test function `z`, the
Rayleigh set of `U_z` contains a positive value. It stands for the dilation
floor lemma of wave item L6-d at `V = Gamma * z`
(`VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor`); it is discharged under the section's
hypotheses in `SpatialOccupationCompleted` (`rayleighFloor_of_homog`, with the
completed wrapper `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper`). Disclosure: since `U_z` is bounded (proved here), this input
is equivalent to `lambda_z(1)^2 > 0` for every such `z`, that is to the
positivity claim of part (i) itself; the Lean content of part (i) beyond the
input is the finiteness, the transfer of positivity to every `c > 0` (through
`Gamma * (c z) = c U_z`) and the Lipschitz bounds. The TeX's positivity route
is different: a positive rate of a smooth test with mean `c U_z` through
`P:variational-unmasked-rate` and `P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines
57-62). The input is satisfiable (`rayleighFloor_volume`: `Gamma` =
Lebesgue measure, an unrestricted constant covariance outside `H:homog`:
it scales like `c^d`, i.e. `alpha = 0`, and it is not spatial white noise,
which is `Gamma = delta_0`) and fails for `Gamma = 0` (refutation
`FloorZeroCovariance`). The boundedness of `U_z` comes from the Gaussian
envelope (`VariationalMean.conv_le`), not from `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
as in the TeX (lines 60-61).

Part (ii). `spatial_static_score_paper` states `E:spatial-static-score` in
the existential form (the owner's decision 2 of wave L6): `B_Gamma(z,z)` is
finite, the Rayleigh set defining `lambda_z(1)` is nonempty and bounded
above, and every `y < lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z)` is exceeded by
`I_Psi - v_Psi/2` for some `Psi` in `C_pos` whose rate and time cost
integrand are integrable on `(0,1)`. This is equivalent to the TeX display
whenever `S_1^pos` is a finite supremum; `spatial_static_score_sSup_paper`
gives the display itself, `lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) <= S_1^pos`, on
the named input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` (boundedness above of
`VariationalRate.score1Set`, that is of
`{I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, word for word the boundedness claim of
`P:variational-positive-scores`, `integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines
272-274, whose manuscript proof, lines 309-325, uses `T:full-upper`; Lean
proves it deterministically in wave L8, `L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed`). Part
(ii) uses neither the floor nor `Gamma != 0`. The proof follows the TeX:
`Psi_n = f_n (x) z` (`ctrl`, in `C_pos` by `ctrl_mem`), mean
`k_n(s) U_z` (`mean_ctrl`), rate `lambda_z(k_n(s))` (`rate_ctrl`), cost
`(int_0^1 f_n k_n) int z U_z` (`rawCost_ctrl`), `k_n -> 1` with
`0 <= k_n <= 1` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` via
`TemporalEquilibrium.potential_eq_one`), `int f_n k_n -> M_a`, and the
limit of the scores (`score_tendsto`); `ctrl_genuine` shows that every
Rayleigh set of `Psi_n` is nonempty and bounded and every integrand is
integrable, so no score is a junk value.

Two bridges connect this module to `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`:
`pairing_eq_spatialPair` proves that the extended pairing
`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` and the real iterated integral
`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair` agree (and are finite) for continuous,
nonnegative, compactly supported functions and locally finite `Gamma`, and
`isUnitH1_of_unitTest` shows that a real unit test of `SpatialFourierBound`
with its classical gradient is a unit `H^1` pair. The weak gradient of a test
function (`VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test`), the radius lemma
(`VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn`) and the score set, `S1Bdd`, `S1pos`
(`VariationalRate`) are shared with other modules and documented there.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: local finiteness of `Gamma` (`Gamma_radon`,
for Tonelli in `B_Gamma`); integrability of every integrand; nonemptiness and
boundedness of every Rayleigh set whose supremum is used; finiteness of
`B_Gamma(z,z)` before `toReal`. Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0` in
both wrappers (part (i) relies on it only through `RayleighFloor`), and the
fields of `H:homog` other than `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral`,
`Gamma_radon`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`.

Proof-route differences: (1) the cutoff is
`cut_n(t) = smoothTransition((n+4)t - 1) smoothTransition((n+4)(1-t) - 1)`
instead of `chi(1/(nt)) chi(1/(n(1-t)))` (lines 66-72); `fn = f_a cut_n`
has the properties the proof uses (smooth, vanishing near the endpoints,
nonzero, `0 <= f_n <= f_a`, `f_n -> f_a`); monotonicity in `n` is not proved
or used; (2) dominated convergence replaces the monotone convergence of
lines 75-77 and 87-88; (3) the TeX's floor `c_0 <= k_n(s)` (line 78) is not
needed, because `lambda_z^2` is globally Lipschitz and `lambda_z` therefore
continuous on `R` (`lam_continuous`); (4) the mean and cost of `f_n (x) z` are
unconditional identities of Bochner integrals. Not formalized: the positivity
of `B_Gamma(z,z)` (lines 88-91), which the stated bound does not need; the
identifications of `lambda`, `I_Psi`, `v_Psi` named above; the finiteness of
`S_1^pos` (the named input `S1Bdd`; proved in wave L8, `L8Completed`). Constant potentials
(`rayleighSet_const`, `lamSq_const`) support the satisfiability check and
the refutations (`refutations/spatial-static-controls/`: the floor fails for
`Gamma = 0`, the Lipschitz constant `M/2` is false, `lambda` is not
Lipschitz on `[0,1]`, positivity fails for `z = 0`).

## SpectralMassIdentity (whole result)

Proves that the spectral-mass constant `R_alpha` of `E:intro-spectral-mass`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lines
528-532: `B_1` the unit ball of `R^d` and
`R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`) is exactly the resolvent at
`1`, `R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2)`, and hence that
`R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha` for `q > 0`. The second identity is the
display in the proof of `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`, lines 149-155). That
proof cites "the deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
`L:damped-homogeneous-norms`" (main file, lines 853-860:
`int mu(dxi)/(a^2+norm(xi)^2) = alpha V a^(alpha-2) int_0^inf u^(alpha-1)/(1+u^2) du`
with `V = mu(B_1)`) together with `E:intro-spectral-mass`. The value of the
radial integral, `pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`, is not written in the TeX; it is
proved here. With the identity, the module states `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
with the manuscript's constant `R_alpha` (`spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper`),
so that lemma is now formalized as printed (statement lines 101-111 of
`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex`, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound` at
lines 106-109).

Abstractions. `ralpha mu alpha` is the formula of line 531 verbatim, with
`B_1` the open unit ball `Metric.ball 0 1` (the same expression as the
hypothesis `hRdef` of the `IntervalScalar` and `IntervalScalarCompleted`
wrappers). The TeX does not say open or closed; for a locally finite
`alpha`-homogeneous `mu` with `alpha > 0` the two balls have the same mass,
but that equality is not stated in Lean and is not needed. `R_Gamma(q)` is
`SpectralHomog.resolvent mu q`, the Bochner integral of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`.

Hypotheses. The general theorems (`resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
`resolvent_eq_ralpha`, `hRdef_iff_resolvent`) assume a locally finite `mu`
with `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for measurable `A` and `c > 0`
(`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`; the sentence of main lines
851-852) and `0 < alpha < 2`. The `_paper` wrappers assume `H:homog`
(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`) and nothing else;
`Gamma = 0` is allowed (then `mu = 0` and both sides are `0`), as in the lemma
("allowing `Gamma = 0`", line 103). The homogeneity is derived by
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and `0 < alpha < 2` by
`alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`. Fields of `H:homog` used by
`resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper` and `hRdef_iff_resolvent_paper` (checked against
every lemma they call: `alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`,
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, `resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
`resolvent_eq_ralpha`): `alpha_range`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `mu_radon`,
and `mu_tempered`, `spectral`, `scaling` (through
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Carried but unused by these two: `dim`,
`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`,
`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`. `spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper` uses the
fields of `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound_paper` (listed in that
section: `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `Gamma_radon`, `mu_radon`,
`spectral`, `mu_tempered`, `scaling`) and `alpha_range`; carried but unused:
`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`.
Supplied inputs: none.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values. The integrability of
`1/(1+norm(xi)^2)` (and of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`) against `mu` is a conjunct of
each identity, so no identity holds through the Lean value `0` of a
non-integrable Bochner integral; this is the TeX's "`< infinity`" of line 154.
`mu(B_1) < infinity` by local finiteness, so `(mu(B_1)).toReal` is not a junk
value, and `sin(pi alpha/2) > 0` for `0 < alpha < 2`, so the division is
genuine. `ralpha` itself is defined for all real `alpha`; outside `(0,2)` it
is only a formula and no theorem here uses it there.

Proof route (differs from the TeX, same conclusion). The TeX uses polar
coordinates. Lean uses the layer-cake formula (as in
`SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq`, which proves finiteness): for
`0 < t < 1` the level set `{1/(1+norm(xi)^2) > t}` is the open ball of radius
`sqrt((1-t)/t)` (`levelset_eq_ball`; empty for `t >= 1`), whose mass is
`((1-t)/t)^(alpha/2) V` (`SpectralHomog.measure_ball`), and the real Beta
integral `int_0^1 t^(-a) (1-t)^a dt = a pi/sin(pi a)` for `0 < a < 1`
(`beta_real`, from Mathlib's complex Beta function and the reflection formula)
at `a = alpha/2`. `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)` is
`SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label
(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Consequences recorded here. `hRdef_iff_resolvent(_paper)`: the hypothesis
`R = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` carried by the `IntervalScalar` and
`IntervalScalarCompleted` wrappers is equivalent to `R = R_Gamma(1)`; those
wrappers are unchanged. The general form of `L:spatial-fourier-bound` with
constant `R_Gamma(1)` stays `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound` and
`spatial_fourier_bound_paper`. Not formalized: nothing of
`E:intro-spectral-mass` or of the display at lines 149-155 is left out.

Refutations (`refutations/spectral-mass-identity/`): `SinFactorTwo`
(`sin(pi alpha/2)` instead of `2 sin(pi alpha/2)` in `R_alpha`, with `mu`
Lebesgue on `R^1`, `alpha = 1`), `ExponentSign` (`q^(2-alpha)` instead of
`q^(alpha-2)`, same `mu`, `q = 2`), `AlphaPositive` (the identity without
`alpha > 0`, at `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`, where `R_Gamma(1) = 1` and
Lean's `R_0` is `0`), `FourierBoundAlphaZero` (the `R_alpha` form of the bound
under the general theorem's hypotheses without `alpha > 0`, with `Gamma`
Lebesgue, `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`; outside `H:homog`). `AlphaPositive` and
`FourierBoundAlphaZero` are controls of Lean's totalized division outside the
manuscript's domain, not convention-independent counterexamples: at
`alpha = 0`, which `H:homog` excludes and where the TeX gives `R_alpha` no
value, `R_0` is the quotient `0/0`, undefined as an ordinary quotient, and
Lean's convention `x/0 = 0` makes it `0`. The continuous extension of
`alpha pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` at `alpha = 0` is `1`; with it `R_0 = 1`, the
identity holds at the witness and the bound holds there (`1 <= 2`).

## StaticPhaseCauchy (proof steps of `P:static-phase-all-orders`, analytic inputs supplied)

Formalizes the complex-analytic, scalar and Banach-space steps of the proof
of `P:static-phase-all-orders` (All regularized static phase orders) of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX;
statement lines 2577-2605, proof lines 2607-2683; all line numbers in this
section refer to that file). The proposition is an operator and stochastic
statement. Every row below is either a step proved with nothing supplied or
a step row of `E:all-static-phase-orders` (lines 2589-2595) or
`E:all-static-phase-sum` (lines 2599-2604) whose operator and Gaussian
inputs are supplied hypotheses (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker
than the labelled statement). It extends the existing proof-step rows of
`SeriesType` for this proposition (the elementary series bound of lines
2670-2679), which `all_static_phase_sum_step` uses.

Constants (nothing supplied): `I_a` and `delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)}` of
`L:complex-phase` (lines 2298-2299), with `I_a` proved integrable and
positive for `a < 2` (the TeX uses `a = alpha/2` in `(0,1)`), so `delta_a`
is a genuine positive number; `A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2)`
(lines 2585-2587); `d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha)` of `E:fock-sandwich`
(lines 2484-2488).

Steps (nothing supplied): Cauchy's estimate for an entire map with values
in a complete complex normed space, operator-valued included (lines
2616-2624), and the coefficient bound `||C_n|| <= M (d/c)^n` in the TeX's
form, quantified over every `d' >= d`, `d' > 0` (this covers the TeX's
`R_alpha = 0` case of line 2608 without dividing by zero); the arithmetic at
`lambda = n/h` (lines 2631-2641): `d_n <= 2 sqrt(2n) sqrt(R)`, the display of
lines 2636-2638, `100 n <= 200^n`, `n! <= n^n`; the pointwise Fourier
multiplier form of the norm comparisons of lines 2632-2633 (the integration
against the Fourier transform is not formalized); the exponent identity of
`E:all-static-phase-sum`.

Step rows. `E:all-static-phase-orders` at fixed cutoffs
(`static_phase_order_cutoff`) and after both cutoff removals
(`static_phase_all_orders_step`, wrapper `static_phase_all_orders_paper`),
and `E:all-static-phase-sum` (`all_static_phase_sum_step`, wrapper
`all_static_phase_sum_paper`). Abstractions: a complex Banach space stands
for the cutoff space `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` and a real Banach space for
`L^2(Omega; X_(1/h))`; the phase propagator is an entire map `F` from the
complex coupling to the bounded operators, its argument `v` is the initial
phase `S_b(f,g)` times the vacuum, and the phase norms are real numbers
`z1`, `zc m b`, `z`, `N1` named by the inputs. The supplied inputs are:
entireness of the phase entries in the coupling (lines 2616-2617); the
circle bound `100 e^(2 lambda h)` from `L:fock-form` and `L:complex-phase`
with `a = alpha/2` (lines 2611-2614), stated for every `d' >= d_n`,
`d' > 0`, which `L:complex-phase` gives from the sandwich bound of
`L:fock-form` (a sandwich bound with constant `d_N` holds with every larger
constant; the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of `L:fock-form` is
`FockForm.fock_form_paper`,
with the spatial column bound supplied, and the scalar steps of
`L:complex-phase` are in `ComplexPhaseScalar`, with its own supplied inputs;
their combination into the propagator bound is not formalized); the
identification of the coefficient with the cutoff Duhamel
phase via `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 2625-2630; proved in `HermiteWordFock`
for one Gaussian coordinate per color only, while the phase words use `m`
coordinates per color) together with the norm
comparison `||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h)` (line 2632); `||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <=
||(f,g)||_(1/h)` (line 2633; the contraction `||S_b(f,g)||_lambda <=
||(f,g)||_lambda` is implicit in the TeX); the cutoff removals `b ->
infinity` and `m -> infinity` (lines 2643-2667) as convergence of the norms
along natural-number cutoffs (the TeX proves strong convergence, which
implies it); and the free bound `||Z_0(h)||_(1/h) <= sqrt(e) ||(f,g)||_(1/h)`
(line 2679). No input assumes a conclusion.

The wrappers state the section's standing class as in
`IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper` (lines 2054-2066): locally finite
`mu, Gamma` on `R^3`, `0 < alpha < 2`, `R = R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2
sin(pi alpha/2))`; evenness, positive definiteness and scaling of `Gamma`
enter only through the supplied inputs. Carried and not used (underscore
hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs): in `static_phase_all_orders_paper`,
local finiteness of `mu` and `Gamma`, `0 < alpha` and the formula for `R`
(the step holds for every real `R` and `alpha < 2`); in
`all_static_phase_sum_paper`, local finiteness (`0 < alpha` and the formula
for `R` are used there, to get `0 <= alpha` and `R_alpha >= 0`).

Junk values: `delta_a` is not a junk value (`I_a` is a proved-integrable
positive integral); every real power has a positive base or a nonnegative
base with a positive exponent; there is no division by `d_N`; summability
is proved, not assumed through `tsum`. `sqrt(R)` is the real square root;
in the wrappers `R = R_alpha >= 0`.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the regularized Duhamel phases
`Z_n^eps(h)` themselves, their being Gaussian polynomials of degree at most
`n`, the uniformity in `eps` (it is that of the inputs), the convergence of
`sum sigma^n Z_n^eps(h)` as an `L^2` phase identified with the Duhamel
series (Lean proves absolute convergence of the abstract series), the lemma
`L:complex-phase` (its scalar and weighted-block-map deductions are in
`ComplexPhaseScalar`, with inputs supplied), the propagator bound built from
it and `L:fock-form` (the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of
`L:fock-form` is in `FockForm` with the spatial column bound supplied), and the
cutoff-removal arguments.
The conclusions are the two displays for the quantities named by the
inputs.

## SymplecticFree (narrower result: `J_E`, the duality-form identification and symplectic preservation on `E` not formalized; force skewness only at the `L^2` level; free-group data and Young convergence supplied)

Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
`a284420` (statement lines 30-60, proof lines 62-133; all line numbers in
this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).

What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
frequency, zero included (lines 79-81), the per-frequency group law and the
reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 120-122). At nonzero frequency
the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 40-41 and 88-91:
abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 45-49) and
`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 53-58) in general form and as
exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).

Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along
the cocompact filter of `R^d`: exactly the properties that lines 103-122
state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
of lines 105-110). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for
`P:constant-young-linear` applied on `L(E)` (lines 91-98): along some
nontrivial filter of finite node lists `(n, p)` whose nodes `p 0, ..., p n`
lie eventually in `[s,t]`, the left Young sums of `X` converge in operator
norm to `U(t,s) - I`. The node lists need not be partitions: ordered nodes,
the endpoints `p 0 = s`, `p n = t` and a vanishing mesh are not required, so
the condition does not characterize the Young evolution; convergence as the
mesh of genuine partitions tends to zero implies it, so it is no stronger
than its source. The Young evolution
itself is not constructed: `U` is any operator family with this property.
The wrappers take `H:homog` as the standing hypothesis; it is used only
through `d >= 1`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E != 0` (on the zero space every
operator has norm `0`, and `||S_E(h)|| >= 1` fails), `d >= 1` (from
`H:homog`; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the nodes lying
in `[s,t]`. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the
wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): `theta`, the Hoelder
bounds and `X(0) = 0` (they are the hypotheses of the supplied Young input)
in both baseline wrappers, and `T > 0` in the single-path wrapper
`symplectic_compact_young_baseline_paper` (the product wrapper has the
horizon `B` and no positivity hypothesis); `H:homog` and smoothness beyond
continuity in `symplectic_force_skew_paper`.

Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 110-112)
is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact
closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the
norm bound of lines 114-119 is proved for each `z` by a limit along the
filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through `M^T J_symp M = (det M)
J_symp` for every `2 x 2` matrix. Helpers that serve only this route are
labelled auxiliary.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the operator `J_E` (bounded,
isometric, skew-adjoint, `J_E^2 = -I`), the identity `omega = <., J_E .>_E`
with its duality form (lines 32-39, 63-68), the preservation of `omega` by
`S_E` on all of `E` (the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity,
lines 82-86), the identification of the `H^(1/2)`-`H^(-1/2)` duality with
the `L^2` integral and the estimate `||bu||_(H^(-1/2)) <=
||b||_infinity ||u||_(H^(1/2))` (line 88), the construction of `S_E`,
`tau_y` and the reversal with the properties of `FreeWaveData`, the Young
evolution, and the remark that a zero length gives `P_j = I` (lines 129-130).
The two displays are stated exactly as in the TeX, for the supplied objects.

## TemporalEquilibrium (whole result)

Formalizes the section `S:temporal-equilibrium`
(`notes/integrated_temporal_equilibrium.tex` at `a284420`): Lemma
`L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` (recurrence, Beta-Gamma identity, duplication) and
Lemma `L:temporal-equilibrium` (positivity, `L^1(0,1) ∩ L^2(0,1)`, the
potential identity `E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` for every `s` in
`[0,1]`, endpoints included, and the mass `E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`).
Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The manuscript's `Gamma_E` is Mathlib's
`Real.Gamma`; `gammaE_integral` records that for `x > 0` it equals the
manuscript's integral, which converges and is positive. `Beta` is defined as
the manuscript's integral over `(0,1)`, and `Beta_eq_betaIntegral` identifies
it with Mathlib's `Complex.betaIntegral`. `density` is the manuscript's `f_a`
with `r = (1-a)/2` written out; it is a total function on the reals, and only
its values on `(0,1)` are used. `L^p(0,1)` is `MemLp` for
`volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1)`. Every evaluation of an ordinary integral that
the manuscript states includes the integrability of its integrand, since
the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is `0`; the evaluated
auxiliary `lintegral`s establish finite nonnegative values, while the
general reflection and splitting identities do not themselves assert
finiteness. The kernel `|s-t|^(-a)` uses Lean's `rpow`, whose value at
`t = s` is irrelevant on a null set. Hypotheses that are carried but unused:
`x > 0` in `gamma_beta_duplication` (the general version needs none) and
`a < 1` in `density_sq_integrableOn` (square integrability needs only
`a > 0`). The proof route differs from the TeX, though the statements do not.
The TeX expands hypergeometric series. Lean proves the Euler-type identity
`int_0^t (t-u)^(-2r) u^(r-1) (1-u)^(r-1) du = Beta(r,1-2r) [t(1-t)]^(-r)`
by the Möbius substitution `u = tv/(1-t+tv)` and then applies a Tonelli
swap. This gives the TeX's incomplete-Beta formula for the left part; the
right part and the endpoints follow by reflection and splitting at `s`. The
remark that the mass "has not been renormalized" is a statement about the
manuscript, not a formula, so it is not formalized. The use of
`L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` in `notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex` is
outside this module. `normalizer_eq_pi_div_sin` is an extra remark that is
not in the TeX.

## TerminalWick (narrower result: `L:terminal-wick` for real `r` only, comparison per mixed moment only, chain measures specified by their masses, not constructed; inputs supplied and an added measurability restriction)

Formalizes `L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `a284420`; the chain measure `E:terminal-chain-measure`, lines 3585-3598; the
statement, lines 3600-3645, with the displays `E:terminal-term-majorant`
(3611-3615), `E:terminal-wick-formula` (3619-3622) and
`E:terminal-pairing-integral` (3624-3637); the proof, lines 3647-3699), built on
`FiniteWick`, with every stated conclusion proved for real `r` and two inputs
left outside Lean, and one added hypothesis (3). (1) Supplied: `hmeas`, the a.e. strong measurability of
`z -> prod_j W(z_j)` as an `L^2(Omega)`-valued map for each `nu n`. In the TeX it
follows from the cell-wise mean-square continuity ("the product is strongly
measurable in `L^2` on the stated pieces", lines 3657-3659); it is assumed here,
almost everywhere only, so it is no stronger than the TeX's claim. (2) Not
constructed: the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}`. The general theorems take
arbitrary finite measures `nu n` on `n`-tuples of points; the wrappers take
finite measures on `n`-tuples of points of `[0,T] x R^d` (`Pt d T`) with total
mass `chainMass d n T`. `chainMass d n T` is the lower integral of
`chainWeight d n T`, the recursion on the last vertex of
`1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) prod_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(R^d)` with `s_{n+1} = T` and the wave
Green measures `WaveGreen.waveGreen d` (in `d = 3` the module's documented
choice of surface measure). Lean proves `chainMass d n T = T^(2n)/(2n)!` for
`d in {1,2,3}`, `T >= 0` (`chainMass_eq`, from `G_h(R^d) = h` and the recursion
`M_{n+1}(T) = int_0^T (T-t) M_n(t) dt`, lines 3648-3651), but not that this is
the total mass of the measure `E:terminal-chain-measure` (a Tonelli and
pushforward identity), since that measure is not built. Only the total masses of
the `nu n` are used, so every conclusion holds for any finite measures with
these masses, in particular for `g_n^{T,x}` once constructed; the point `x`
enters only through the measures. (3) Added restriction, not in the
manuscript: `hK`, the joint (Borel) measurability of `(p, q) -> K p q` on
pairs of points of `[0,T] x R^d`, a hypothesis of `mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings`,
`integrable_pairWeight` and `terminal_wick_paper`, used only to split the
integral of the pairing sum into the separate pairing integrals and to prove
each pairing integrand integrable. The TeX assumes bounded variance and joint
mean-square continuity only on the open cells of a finite partition of
`[0,T]`; these leave the covariance at the cut times unrestricted, so `hK`
does not follow from them (a field that vanishes off one cut time `c` and
equals `1_A(y) Z` there, with `A` not Borel and `Z` standard Gaussian, meets
every TeX hypothesis and the supplied `hmeas`, but its covariance is not
measurable). The wrapper is therefore narrower than the lemma by this
restriction; `terminal_wick_mono_paper`, `mixed_moment_odd`,
`mixed_moment_nonneg` and `terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` do not take it. `Y_n` is `chainIntegral nu hW n`, the
Bochner integral in Mathlib's `Lp R 2 P` of `prodL2 hW z`, the `L^2` class of
`prod_j W(z_j)`; `E[Y_m Y_n]` is the integral of `Y_m(omega) Y_n(omega)`, equal to
the `L^2` inner product. `V = sup_p K(p,p)` (the TeX's `sup E|W|^2`; under
`CenteredGaussianField` the one-point law of `W(p)` is `multivariateGaussian 0` of the `1 x 1` matrix `K(p,p)`) is the
supremum `iSup` with `BddAbove` as hypothesis (the TeX's `V < infinity`), so it is
a genuine supremum, and `V^(n/2)` is a real power. The pairing integral
`T^K_{m,n,D}` is `pairingIntegral nu K m n D`, the integral against
`nu m x nu n` of `prod_{{a,b} in D} K(tau_a, tau_b)` with `tau` the
concatenation (`Fin.append`) of the two tuples, which carry both time and
space. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: positive semidefiniteness of the
covariance matrices (part of `CenteredGaussianField`), finiteness of each
`nu n`, `BddAbove` of the variances, and `T > 0` (the measurability `hK` of
the covariance is not implicit in the TeX; see (3)). Hypotheses carried but unused (checked by
recompiling both wrapper proofs with them removed): in `terminal_wick_paper`,
`IsProbabilityMeasure P` and `MeanSquareCellContinuous K` (which stands behind
the supplied `hmeas`); in `terminal_wick_mono_paper`, both probability
instances, both cell-continuity hypotheses, `d in {1,2,3}` and the masses.
Proof-route differences: the `L^2` bound of the product uses the Wick formula and
the count of pairings (`FiniteWick.CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le`) instead
of Hoelder's inequality (lines 3651-3656), with the same bound; the Wick formula
comes from `FiniteWick` (Gaussian integration by parts, not the moment generating
function); Fubini is applied through `integral_inner` and `integral_prod_symm`;
absolute convergence is by comparison with `sum c^n/n!` through
`sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/n!` instead of the ratio test (lines 3695-3697).
Narrower conclusions: absolute convergence of `sum_n r^n Y_n` is stated for real
`r` only (the TeX also states complex `r`; a complexified `L^2` is not set up);
the comparison sentence ("compares all finite partial-order second moments",
lines 3641-3642) is stated for each mixed moment `E[Y_m Y_n]`; second moments
of finite partial sums are not stated as such. The majorant is
proved for every `n`, including `n = 0` (the TeX states `n >= 1`). Junk values:
`chainIntegral` would be `0` for a non-integrable integrand, but the wrapper
proves integrability from `hmeas`; the bound `norm_chainIntegral_le` and the
summability `summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral` need no measurability because
they also hold for the junk value; every pairing integrand is proved integrable,
so `pairingIntegral` is a genuine integral in the wrapper. Cross-item discharge:
`terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (and the last conjunct of `terminal_wick_paper`)
proves both fields of `UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput` for the family
`Y_n` and every real `r` when `K >= 0`. Not formalized: the construction of
`g_n^{T,x}` and of its density `g_n` of `E:expansion` in `d = 1, 2`; the
symmetrization paragraph (lines 3677-3683, identification with the symmetrized
convention of `E:expansion`); the `d = 3` Green-regularization paragraph
(lines 3685-3691, agreement with the source's fixed-noise convention); and
complex `r`. No conclusion of the module uses the two omitted paragraphs. The
route definitions `chainWeightReal` and `chainMassReal` (the same recursion
with each Green mass `G_h(R^d)` replaced by `h`) are public but not listed as
claims; they appear in the statements of the rows below. Refutations
(`refutations/terminal-wick/`), all scalar controls without junk-value
reliance and without a Gaussian field: `ChainMassSimplex` (`M_n(T) = T^n/n!`,
forgetting the Green masses; `d = 1`, `n = 1`, `T = 1`), `ChainMassFactorial`
(`M_n(T) = T^(2n)/(n!)^2`; `d = 2`, `n = 1`, `T = 1`) and `MajorantFactor`
(`sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/(2n)!`; `n = 2`).

## TimeCompletion (whole result)

Covers two modules, `TimeCompletion` and `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, on
`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `a284420`. It formalizes
`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 141-156, display `E:masked-time-schur` at
150-152, proof 158-181) with the completion `H_a` constructed. It re-issues
`L:masked-trig-products` (lines 347-374) and `L:masked-continuous-wave`
(lines 378-423, display `E:masked-continuous-wave` at 385-389) in this
concrete `H_a`, with nothing supplied. Standing hypotheses: `T > 0` and
`0 < a < 1` (the section's `a = alpha0`, lines 4-7). The section also assumes
`H:homog` and `Gamma != 0`, but lines 5-7 say the purely temporal estimates
hold independently of `Gamma`. These lemmas are purely temporal, so neither
hypothesis is assumed.

What is constructed. `L2fun T` is complex `L^2(0,T)` as a space of
functions (`MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`). On it,
`TimeSchur.timeForm` (`<f,g>_a = int int f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)`) is a
Hermitian sesquilinear form (`conj_timeForm`, `timeForm_add_right`,
`timeForm_smul_right`) and is positive semidefinite (`timeForm_re_nonneg`).
These are the axioms of a pre-inner product (`core`; the arguments are
swapped because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first
slot). `Ha p` is Mathlib's `UniformSpace.Completion` of the resulting
pre-Hilbert space `Pre p`, so it is a complex Hilbert space, and functions at
seminorm distance zero are identified (`coe_eq_of_ae`, the null quotient).
`emb p` is the inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. Its squared norm is
`Re timeForm a T f f` (`emb_norm_sq`). This is faithful to the TeX's "null-quotient completion" for the following reason. The TeX completes the
real compact smooth tests and then complexifies. `dense_span_realTestSet`
proves that the complex span of the images of the real tests supported in
`(0,T)` is dense in `Ha p`. So `Ha p` is the closure of the complexified
tests, and its norm on a test is the TeX's form. `H_a` is built directly over
`C`. The TeX's real space is represented by the real functions of
`emb_norm_sq_real` and the positivity clause, not by a separate real
Hilbert space.

The paper wrapper `masked_time_completion_paper` has exactly the hypotheses
`0 < a < 1`, `T > 0` and states, in eight conjuncts:
- positivity on real compact smooth tests, with integrability of the
  integrand;
- separability of `Ha p`;
- `E:masked-time-schur` for `||emb f||`;
- the continuous linear extension `extL2 p` on a.e.-classes of
  `L^2(0,T)`, agreeing with `emb`, with the same constant;
- the complexification clause: `||emb f||^2` equals the complex double
  integral with `f(t) conj f(s)`, it is the sum of the squared norms of the
  real and imaginary parts, and the integrand is integrable;
- for real `g`, `||emb g||^2` equals the real double integral;
- interval amplitudes: a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable amplitude on
  `[c,d]`, extended by zero, lies in `L^2(0,T)` and hence has an image under
  `emb`;
- density of the complex span of the real tests' images.

Proof route and differences from the TeX.
- Positivity follows the TeX (lines 159-172). Gamma subordination
  (`TimeFractional.rpow_neg_eq_subordination`) and the exponential-kernel
  identity `exp_abs_eq` give, for `t != s`,
  `|t-s|^(-a) = int Gamma(a)^(-1) 2 lambda^a 1_(u<=t) e^(-lambda(t-u)) 1_(u<=s) e^(-lambda(s-u)) d lambda du`
  (`kern_eq_mixture`, an identity in `[0, infinity]`). The TeX argues for each
  `lambda` separately. Lean makes one Fubini exchange over
  `[0,T]^2 x (0,infinity) x R` in the general criterion
  `re_form_nonneg_of_mixture` (s-finite measures, nonnegative measurable
  weight and profiles). Absolute integrability comes from the Schur bound,
  as in the TeX (`cross_integrable`). Positivity is proved for every complex
  `f` in `L^2(0,T)`, which is stronger than the TeX's real tests.
- Separability uses the separability of `Lp` (Mathlib) and the Lipschitz
  representative map `ofLp`, not a countable family of tests.
- The TeX extends the inclusion from tests to `L^2` by density. Here `H_a` is
  built over `L^2(0,T)`, so the inclusion is defined on all of `L^2`. The
  density of the tests is proved afterwards by `exists_test_approx`, which
  uses three ingredients: Mathlib's `MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le`; a
  `ContDiffBump` equal to one on `[eta, T-eta]` and supported in
  `[eta/2, T-eta/2]`; and uniform integrability
  (`MemLp.eLpNorm_indicator_le`) for the boundary layer.
- `masked_trig_products_completed_paper` instantiates
  `MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` with `E = Ha p`,
  `V = L2fun T` and `emb p`. `hmem` comes from
  `MaskedModulation.memLp_modeFn`, and `hnorm` from `emb_norm_sq`.
- `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper` instantiates
  `MaskedContinuousWave.masked_continuous_wave_paper` in the same way. Its
  `hmem` quantifies over every `A` in `C^1(I)`. For each such `A`,
  `MaskedModulation.envelope_of_contDiffOn` (using `h > 0`) gives continuity
  and boundedness on `I`, and `memLp_modeFn` gives membership.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
- `L^2(0,T)` is `MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`, and `[0,T]` versus
  `(0,T)` is immaterial.
- The kernel's diagonal value `0^(-a) = 0` is irrelevant, because the
  diagonal is null for the product measure (`ae_ne_diag`). The mixture
  identity is used only off the diagonal.
- Integrability on `[0,T]^2` is a conjunct of the wrapper's double-integral
  conclusions (items 1 and 5), so no Bochner integral is Lean's junk `0`.
- `mixWeight` uses `|lambda|^a`, equal to `lambda^a` on the only values that
  `mixMeasure` charges, so no `rpow` of a negative base occurs.
- `M` and `D` in the trig-products wrapper are suprema of bounded nonempty
  sets (`envelope_of_contDiffOn`).

Hypotheses carried but unused:
- `tsupport f` in `(0,T)` in item 1 of the paper wrapper (positivity holds on
  all of `L^2(0,T)`).
- `h <= 1` in `masked_trig_products_completed_paper`.

`T > 0` is needed to build `Ha p` (it is a field of `TimeParams`), although
the bounds themselves do not use it.

Not formalized: a separate real Hilbert space `H_a` and its abstract
complexification (both are represented as described above). The `H_a`-valued
Schwartz functions and the noise of `P:masked-noise-completion` are also not
formalized.

The two calibration lemmas `timeForm_one` and `norm_sq_waveFn_cc_zero` give
the exact value at the constant function and at `1_[0,h]`. They have no
manuscript label and are used by the refutations
(`refutations/time-completion/`,
`refutations/masked-continuous-wave-completed/`).

## TypeContinuity (narrower result: `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and `C:static-moment-constant-continuity` for an abstract moment function, the solution moments not constructed and their identification not formalized; `L:positive-series-type` whole)

Formalizes the section `S:temporal-type-continuity` of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` (main file, at `a284420`)
together with the lemma it uses from the preceding section
`S:near-static-lower`. The section's parameters (lines 7062-7069) are
`nu = 3 - alpha`, `a_max = min(1, 2 - alpha)`, `beta(a) = 4 - alpha - a`,
`kappa(a) = beta(a)/nu` and `kappa_st = (4 - alpha)/nu`. In Lean they are
`nuOf`, `amaxOf`, `betaOf`, `kappaOf` and `kappaSt`.

**`L:positive-series-type`** (statement lines 7222-7234, proof lines
7236-7263) is formalized in full by `positive_series_type_paper`, with the
lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied:

- The hypotheses are `nu >= 1`, `c_k >= 0` and `c_0 = 1`. "`F(z) < inf` for
  every `z >= 0`" is stated as summability of `k -> c_k z^k`.
- The type `tau` (`seriesType`) is an `EReal` limsup, with no truncation and
  no boundedness side condition.
- The coefficient type `K` (`coeffType`) is in `[0, inf]`. Its terms
  `((k!)^nu c_k)^(1/k)` are nonnegative reals, so `ENNReal.ofReal` does not
  truncate them. The `k = 0` term (`1/0 = 0` in Lean) does not affect the
  limsup.
- Both directions are proved, and the equality is stated with `K.toReal`
  together with `K < top`.
- Proof-route difference: the first half uses the eventual bound
  `F(z) <= e^(L z^(1/nu))` instead of the TeX's global
  `C_L e^(L z^(1/nu))`. This suffices because the test points
  `(nu k/L)^nu` tend to infinity.
- `coeffType_exp_family` and `seriesType_exp_family` check non-vacuity:
  `c_k = A^k/(k!)^nu` gives `K = A` and `tau = nu A^(1/nu)`.

**`P:moment-growth-logconvex`** (statement lines 7516-7528, proof lines
7530-7572) and **`C:static-moment-constant-continuity`** (statement lines
7574-7593, proof lines 7595-7606) are proved with every conclusion, from
named inputs. The moment `E[u^(a)(T,x)^p]` is an abstract real function
`mom p a T` at a fixed point `x`. `mom p 0` is the static moment, as the TeX
defines `u^(0) = U` (lines 7072-7074). Because `x` is fixed, the spatial
stationarity used at line 7541 is not needed. The rates of
`E:moment-growth-types` (lines 7505-7514) are `EReal` limsup and liminf
(`growthUpper`, `growthLower`). Statements about real values use `toReal`
only together with a proved finiteness and positivity, so no junk `toReal`
enters.

The inputs are the fields of `TypeContinuityInputs`, each no stronger than
its source:

- `L0_pos` and `static_law`: `E:static-ratio-input` (lines 7079-7087),
  verbatim.
- `series`: `E:full-moment-positive-series` with nonnegative coefficients
  and `c_0 = 1` (the definition `E:full-moment-coefficients`), for
  `0 <= a < a_max`, from `L:full-moment-coefficient-holder` (lines
  7433-7439). "`< inf`" is stated as summability.
- `holder`: `E:full-moment-coefficient-holder` (lines 7440-7444), verbatim.
- `minorant`: `E:static-minorant-rate` of `P:static-minorant-lower` (lines
  7271-7275), in the equivalent real form "every `y < p^(kappa_st) L_0` is
  eventually below `T^(-kappa(a)) log mom`".
- `full_upper`: `E:full-upper-bound` of `T:full-upper` (lines 3758-3772)
  applied at temporal exponent `a`, as the TeX does at line 7534. The finite
  constant `C R_alpha^(1/(3-alpha))` is merged into one finite `C`.
- `cauchy_schwarz`: `(E u)^2 <= E u^2`, the step at line 7535.

What is proved from these inputs:

- Positivity and finiteness of the rates are derived exactly as in the TeX
  proof (lines 7531-7537), by `upper_rate_pos_fin`; they are not supplied.
- The identification of the type of `F_{p,a}` with `Lambda-bar_p(a)`
  through `z = T^(beta(a))` (lines 7539-7543) is proved by
  `growthUpper_eq_seriesType`, not supplied.
- The corollary's own inputs, `P:static-minorant-lower` and
  `Lambda-bar_p(0) = C_p`, are derived from `minorant` and `static_law`.

Further details:

- Convexity of `log Lambda-bar_p` is stated on `[0, a_max)`, the range of
  the inequality.
- Continuity on `(0, a_max)` is proved with
  `ConvexOn.continuousOn_interior` instead of the TeX's secant slopes
  (lines 7561-7570).
- Standing assumptions: the section's "nonzero spatial covariance in
  `H:homog`" (lines 7062, 7423) is carried as `HomogCovariance` and
  `Gamma != 0`. Only `alpha < 2` is used, which gives `nu >= 1`,
  `a_max > 0` and `beta(a) > 0`. `Gamma != 0` is carried and not used.
- The general forms `growth_logconvex_core` and `static_constant_core` state
  the arguments for an arbitrary family, with positivity and finiteness of
  the rates as hypotheses.
- Every conclusion formula is proved for the abstract moment function; its
  identification with the solution moments is not formalized.
- Not formalized: the inputs above, that is `L:full-moment-coefficient-holder`
  (stochastic diagram limits), the Chen-Hu static law, `T:full-upper`,
  `P:static-minorant-lower` and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the
  solution. Lean also does not show that these inputs are jointly satisfiable.
