## UniformSeriesTail (narrower result: `L:uniform-series-tail` for an abstract `L^2` family with the two facts of `L:terminal-wick` supplied; identification with the terminal-chain terms not formalized)

Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
not formalized. The
fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
convergence", lines 3735-3736). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
last sentence (lines 3725-3726): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
(lines 3738-3745), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
`1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: the regularized family itself (the terms
`Y_n^{eps,delta}` as terms of `L:terminal-wick`) and the application of the
lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; `L:terminal-wick` is in
`TerminalWick`, with its own inputs.

## VariationalDilation (narrower result: `L:variational-control-dilation`, rate and variance identification not formalized)

Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (Radon and Rayleigh
dilation; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines 225-268 at
`a284420`) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules:
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean` (a hand-built real Sobolev
space and the real Rayleigh value set) and
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean` (the control class,
the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma).
The wrapper `variational_control_dilation_paper` states the lemma with the
section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
`H:homog`, modelled by `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, with `a = alpha0`):
for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a bijection of the class with inverse `D_(1/r)`, and the
four identities of `E:variational-dilation-values` hold. Nothing is supplied as
a hypothesis.

Abstractions and why they are faithful.
The class `E:variational-positive-class` (lines 5-10) consists of smooth
functions on `R x R^d` with compact support inside `(0,1) x R^d`, i.e. elements
of `C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d)` extended by zero. `CPos_nonempty` proves that
the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean
`h_{Psi,s}` and the variance `v_Psi` are the
displays `E:compact-raw-mean` and `E:compact-raw-cost`
(`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex` lines 402-412), with
`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)` and `int_0^1` taken over
`Ioo 0 1`. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces, so `WeakSobolev` defines
`H^1(R^d; R)` by weak gradients (`int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi` for every
test function `phi` and direction `v`). It proves that an `L^2` weak gradient
is unique a.e. (`weakGradient_ae_unique`), so a Rayleigh set built from pairs
`(f, g)` is the manuscript's set of `f`.

The rate `lambda_{Psi,s}` is defined in Lean by the real Rayleigh form
`E:variational-real-rayleigh`: `rate = sqrt(sSup R_s)`, where `R_s` is the set
of values `int h_s f^2 - ||grad f||_2^2` over unit `f in H^1(R^d; R)`. The
manuscript's primary definition is `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`, with `E_s` the
spectral bottom of the self-adjoint `-Delta - h_s` on `H^2`. The manuscript
proves that the two agree (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`), but that equality is
**not formalized**, because it needs unbounded self-adjoint operators and
spectral theory. Likewise `v_Psi` is the integral form of
`E:compact-raw-cost`, and its identification with `E W(Psi)^2`
(`L:compact-raw-profile`, which needs the Gaussian noise) is **not
formalized**. The TeX proof itself works with exactly these two forms
(Lebesgue substitution in the pairing, and the real Rayleigh bijection).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
- A Rayleigh trial must have `h_s f^2` integrable. The condition keeps
  Lean's junk value `0` for a non-integrable integral out of the set. For
  the manuscript's `h_s` (`Psi in CPos`, `s in [0,1]`) it is automatic:
  `VariationalMean.isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper` proves that a trial is
  then exactly a unit `f in L^2` with an `L^2` weak gradient, because `h_s`
  is bounded and continuous (`L:variational-global-mean`, formalized in
  `VariationalMean`).
- `Psi` is continuous; this follows from smoothness.
- The identities hold for every real `s`, not only for `s in [0,1]`.

Junk values. Every identity is an exact identity of Bochner integrals and of
`sSup`. It would remain true if an integrand were not integrable, or if the
Rayleigh set were empty or unbounded (Lean's value `0` on both sides). The
companion does not exclude these junk cases. It proves only conditional
transfers, in `variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper`:
- every integrand in the definitions of `h`, `v` and `I` is integrable for
  `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`;
- the Rayleigh sets themselves scale, so a Rayleigh set is nonempty and
  bounded above for `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`.

So if a quantity is a genuine integral or supremum for `Psi`, the identity
relates it to a genuine integral or supremum for `D_r Psi`. For
`s in [0,1]`, `VariationalMean` proves that the integrand of `h_s(x)` is
integrable and that `h_s` is bounded (`L:variational-global-mean`,
`variational_global_mean_paper`), so the mean identity relates genuine
integrals there. That the variance and rate integrands are integrable, and
that the Rayleigh sets are nonempty and bounded above, is not proved in
this module. For `Psi in C_pos` under the section's hypotheses these are
proved in `VariationalRate` (`rawCost_genuine`, `unmasked_rate`); the
identifications `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2` and `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` remain
outside Lean. The
integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries: the TeX proof
(lines 243-250) works with nonnegative integrands and Tonelli and states none
of them. Their rows below say so.

The TeX's square-root step uses positivity of the rates. Lean instead uses
`sqrt(sSup(r^2 S)) = r sqrt(sSup S)`, which holds for every set `S`.

Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0`, and every clause of `H:homog`
except the set scaling. The general theorems assume only the set scaling
`SetScaling` and continuity of `Psi`.

Not formalized:
- `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`; positivity of the
  Rayleigh-form rate is in `VariationalRate`);
- `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2` (`L:compact-raw-profile`; finiteness and positivity
  of the integral form are in `VariationalRate`);
- the mixed-derivative bounds of `L:variational-global-mean` (its display
  is formalized in `VariationalMean`);
- integrability of the integrands of `v` and `I` (that of `h` for
  `s in [0,1]` is in `VariationalMean`), and nonemptiness and
  boundedness of the Rayleigh sets (only their transfer under `D_r` is
  proved);
- the TeX's side remark that `U_r` preserves `H^2` and that
  `H_{D_r Psi,s} U_r = r^2 U_r H_{Psi,s}` (not part of the statement).

The auxiliary definition `VariationalDilation.dilHomeo` (the spatial dilation
as a homeomorphism of `R x R^d`) only names a map used in the proof and has no
row. The structure fields `IsRayleighTrial.memLp_f`, `memLp_g`, `weakGrad`,
`unit` and `integrable_pot` are projections of `IsRayleighTrial` and have no
rows either. Four refutations in `refutations/variational-dilation/` prove
that the following wrong variants are false:
- the mean scaling with `r` in place of `r^2`;
- the variance scaling without the Lebesgue factor (`r^(d+4-alpha)`);
- the rate scaling with `r^2`;
- the bijection with `r > 0` dropped.

## VariationalFloor (foundation: the variational floor)

Five deterministic foundations of wave L6 (item L6-d), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalFloor.lean`. They carry no
manuscript label of their own: they are the facts that the variational rates
of `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` (Section
`S:unmasked-variational`) and the spatial results of
`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (Section
`S:spatial-occupation-foundation`) use, at revision `a284420`. Every
hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. They are consumed by
`VariationalRate`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls` and
`SpatialOccupationCompleted`.

- (F1) `dilation_floor`, `rayleighSet_floor`: the dilation floor. For a
  nonzero locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling
  `Gamma(c A) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` of `H:homog` and `alpha < 2`, and a
  continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `z` with
  `y -> z(x-y)` `Gamma`-integrable for every `x` (so `Gamma * z` is a genuine
  integral, not Lean's junk value `0`), one unit test `f` in `C_c^infinity`,
  an `L^2` weak gradient `g` and one `eps > 0` give
  `eps <= int V f^2 - int norm(g)^2` for every potential `V >= Gamma * z` with
  `V f^2` integrable. The test is `U_l phi / norm(phi)_2` for a fixed bump
  `phi` and small `l`; the potential term is at least
  `l^alpha (int z) Gamma(closed unit ball)/norm(phi)_2^2` (Tonelli in
  `(x, y)` and the scaling of `Gamma` on balls) and the gradient term is
  `l^2 norm(grad phi)_2^2/norm(phi)_2^2`. It is a pure inequality (no limit,
  no supremum). This is the elementary scaling principle behind the
  positivity in `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (TeX lines 150-155), which the
  manuscript obtains instead from the compact trial of
  `P:compact-original-common-trial`; it also discharges the input
  `RayleighFloor` of `SpatialStaticControls`.
- (F2) `measure_ball_pos`, `measure_closedBall_pos`: `Gamma(B_r) > 0` for
  every `r > 0` when `Gamma != 0` has the set scaling (exhaustion by balls
  and scaling: the argument of `L:spatial-static-controls`, occupation file
  lines 89-91).
- (F3) `autocorr_nonneg_of_posDef`: for a real `Q` in `C_c^infinity`,
  `int c_Q dGamma >= 0` when `Gamma` is positive definite in the sense of the
  field `Gamma_posdef` of `H:homog`, where `c_Q = SpatialFourierBound.autocorr Q`
  (`c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx`, the inner integral of `B_Gamma(Q,Q)` in
  `E:spatial-physical-pair`); route: `HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap` and the
  cast of the real pairing to `C`. `autocorr_pos`: `int c_Q dGamma > 0` for
  continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `Q` and nonzero
  locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling (no positive definiteness; TeX
  lines 88-91 and 182-185 of the occupation file).
- (F4) `hasWeakGradient_of_test`, with the gradient field `grad`: a test
  function has its classical gradient as weak gradient
  (`WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient`).
- (F5) `ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero`: for `d >= 1`, an `L^2` function
  with weak gradient `0` is `0` almost everywhere (half (b) of the D8-lite foundation; half (a),
  the density of test functions in the weak-gradient `H^1`, is
  `H1Density.h1TestDense`, wave L7). This is the fact used in `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (occupation
  file lines 180-182); the Lean route differs from the TeX's Fourier-support
  argument: the mollifications `rho_n * f` are smooth with derivative
  `(D rho_n) * f = 0`, hence constant, they converge to `f` almost everywhere,
  and a nonzero constant is not in `L^2(R^d)` for `d >= 1`. The hypothesis
  `d >= 1` is necessary (refutation `ZeroDimension`).

Also `integral_pos_of_pos_zero` and `conv_pos` (positivity of integrals
against such `Gamma`, from F2), and `exists_radius_fn`. Junk values: the
statements involving `conv Gamma z` assume the integrability of
`y -> z(x-y)`; the F3 integral is a genuine integral for locally finite
`Gamma` (`SpatialFourierBound.integrable_autocorr`); the floor's conclusion
is about the Rayleigh value of one explicit trial, not about a supremum.
Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve
only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

## VariationalMean (narrower result: `L:variational-global-mean` without the mixed derivatives; `L:variational-heat-envelope` whole)

Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-heat-envelope` (Gaussian envelope for the
original covariance; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` at `a284420`,
statement lines 23-35, proof 37-62) in full, and the display
`E:variational-global-mean` of Lemma `L:variational-global-mean` (global
regularity of the original mean; statement 64-74, proof 76-96), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalMean.lean`. It reuses the definitions
of `VariationalDilation`: the convolution `conv` (`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int
phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)`), the mean `mean` (`h_{Psi,s}`, `E:compact-raw-mean`) and
the control class `CPos` (`E:variational-positive-class`). The only new
manuscript object is the heat kernel `heatK eps x = (2 pi eps)^(-d/2)
e^(-norm(x)^2/(2 eps))` (lines 25-26). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

The wrappers state the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-5: a nonzero
covariance satisfying `H:homog`, with `a = alpha0`) as
`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and `Gamma != 0`;
the mean is taken with exponent `alpha0`.
`variational_heat_envelope_paper` (with `eps > 0`) gives, for every `x`, the
integrability of `y -> p_eps(x-y)` against `Gamma` (so `(Gamma * p_eps)(x)`,
in particular the value at `0`, is finite), the integrability of the spectral
integrand against `mu`, the identity of `E:variational-heat-envelope` as
complex numbers with no normalization factor, `0 <= (Gamma * p_eps)(x) <=
(Gamma * p_eps)(0)`, and `(Gamma * p_eps)(0) > 0`.
`variational_global_mean_paper` (with `Psi in CPos`) gives real
`M, C_Psi >= 0` with `0 <= h_s(x) <= M` and `|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C_Psi
|s - t|` for `s, t in I = [0,1]` and every `x` (the sup-norm bound of the
display, stated pointwise in `x`). It also gives the integrability of every
integrand in the definition of `h_s(x)`, the continuity of `x -> h_s(x)` and
the integrability of `h_s f^2` for every `f in L^2`.
`variational_global_mean_lipschitz_paper` adds a joint Lipschitz bound on
`I x R^d`; the TeX does not state it.
`isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper` shows that the explicit side condition
`integrable_pot` of `WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic for `h_s`,
`s in [0,1]`.

General forms: `heat_envelope` assumes `Gamma`, `mu` tempered (`IsTempered`)
and the spectral convention `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`, without
`Gamma != 0`; `heat_conv_pos` assumes `Gamma` tempered and `Gamma != 0`;
`heat_identity` assumes only the spectral convention; `global_mean` assumes
`Gamma`, `mu` tempered, the spectral convention, `Psi in CPos` and `a < 1`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `eps > 0`. Finiteness of
`(Gamma * p_eps)(0)` and of `h_s(x)` is stated as integrability of the
integrands. A Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, so
without these conclusions the bounds could hold through that junk value.
`M` and `C_Psi` are nonnegative real numbers.

Hypotheses carried but unused. The wrappers use the `H:homog` fields
`Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered` and `spectral`; the global-mean wrappers also
use `alpha0_lt_one`. `Gamma != 0` is used only for the strict positivity in
`L:variational-heat-envelope`, and the global-mean wrappers carry it unused.
The other fields (`dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_radon`, `mu_even`, `scaling`, `threshold`, `alpha_range`)
are carried, unused.

Proof-route differences.
- The identity of `E:variational-heat-envelope` comes from
  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectral_translated_gauss`: the spectral convention
  applied to one Gaussian Schwartz test, with Mathlib's Gaussian Fourier
  integral. The TeX pairs with an arbitrary Schwartz test and uses
  uniqueness of continuous distributions (lines 48-57).
- Integrability against `Gamma` and `mu` comes from the package's integral
  form of temperedness, not from polynomial ball growth (lines 38-44).
- The bound by the value at `0` follows line 59 but does not use evenness of
  `mu`: the spectral integral is real because it equals the real left side.
- For the mean, `|Psi(u,z)| <= C e^(-norm(z)^2/2)` (spatial support) and the
  envelope at `eps = 1` (`gauss_conv`) bound `Gamma * Psi(u,.)` uniformly, as
  in lines 78-82 for the underived case.
- The change of variables `r = s - u` (lines 84-88) is
  `integral_sub_left_eq_self`. The integral runs over `(-1,1)` rather than
  `R`, since the integrand vanishes outside `(-1,1)` for `s in [0,1]`. The
  time constant is `int_(-1)^1 |r|^(-a) dr = 2/(1-a)` (`a < 1`).
- The Lipschitz bound in time does not differentiate under the integral (the
  TeX's route, lines 82-94). It applies the Lipschitz bound of the smooth,
  compactly supported `Psi` (`ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport`)
  inside both integrals, dominated by the same Gaussian envelope.

Narrower conclusion and not formalized:
- the first sentence of `L:variational-global-mean`, "every mixed time and
  space derivative of `h_s` is globally bounded in space, uniformly on
  compact time intervals" (no derivative of `h_s` is formalized; only the
  display `E:variational-global-mean` on `I = [0,1]`, plus the spatial and
  joint Lipschitz bounds, which are first-order statements without
  derivatives);
- the smoothness of `x -> (Gamma * p_eps)(x)` mentioned in the proof of
  `L:variational-heat-envelope` (lines 44-46), which is not part of its
  statement.

Five refutations in `refutations/variational-mean/` prove that the following
wrong variants are false:
- strict positivity of `(Gamma * p_eps)(0)` without `Gamma != 0`
  (`Gamma = mu = 0`);
- the identity with an extra factor `(2 pi)^(-d)` (`d = 1`, Lebesgue `Gamma`,
  `mu = delta_0`);
- a strict peak `(Gamma * p_eps)(x) < (Gamma * p_eps)(0)` for `x != 0` (same
  example, where the convolution is constant);
- integrability of `|r|^(-a)` on `(-1,1)` with `a < 1` relaxed to `a <= 1`;
- the one-sided constant `1/(1-a)`.

## VariationalRate (narrower result: Rayleigh-form rates and integral-form costs, their spectral and stochastic identification, the operator half of `P:variational-unmasked-rate` and `Q_2 >= S_2^pos` not formalized)

Formalizes the Rayleigh-form part of Proposition `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
(the unmasked Rayleigh rate; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` at
`a284420`, statement lines 98-111, proof 113-164) and Proposition
`P:variational-positive-scores` (intrinsic variational lower bounds;
statement 270-284, proof 286-337) except `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`, in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalRate.lean`. The wrappers state the
section's standing assumptions (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
`H:homog`, `a = alpha0`) as `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
`Gamma != 0`. Reused definitions (`VariationalDilation`): the class `CPos`
(`E:variational-positive-class`), the mean `h_{Psi,s}` (`mean`), the
integral form `v_Psi` of `E:compact-raw-cost` (`rawCost`), the rate
`lambda_{Psi,s}` DEFINED as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum
`E:variational-real-rayleigh` (`rate`) and `I_Psi` (`integratedRate`). New
definitions: `scoreSet a Gamma c = {c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, the
coefficient-one set `score1Set` (`= scoreSet a Gamma 1`), `S1pos = sSup
score1Set`, the test radius `r_0` (`testRadius`) and the named input `S1Bdd`.
These are the package's only score set, `S1Bdd` and `S1pos`;
`SpatialSmoothRatio` and `SpatialStaticControls` use them.

`variational_unmasked_rate_paper` (general form `unmasked_rate`): for
`Psi in C_pos` and `s, t in [0,1]`, the real Rayleigh value set of `h_s` is
nonempty and bounded above with a uniform floor and ceiling
`eps <= lambda_s^2 = sup <= M` (`eps > 0` is the TeX's `eps_0`;
`-M <= E_s <= -eps_0` in the TeX's notation `E_s = -lambda_s^2`);
`|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C |s - t|`; `|lambda_s^2 - lambda_t^2| <= C |s - t|`
(from `abs_sSup_rayleighSet_sub_le`, `|sup R_V - sup R_W| <= norm(V - W)_inf`,
TeX line 156); `sqrt eps <= lambda_s <= sqrt M`;
`|lambda_s - lambda_t| <= C/(2 sqrt eps) |s - t|` (line 158); `lambda` is
integrable on `(0,1)`; and `sqrt eps <= I_Psi <= sqrt M`, so `I_Psi` is a
positive finite integral of an integrable function.
`variational_positive_scores_paper` (general form `positive_scores`), with
nothing supplied: the value sets are nonempty; for every `Psi in C_pos` the
values are genuine (rate integrable, every variance integrand integrable,
`rawCost_genuine`) with `I_Psi > 0` and `v_Psi > 0` (`rawCost_pos`); the
positive test of lines 290-296, `I - v/2 = r_0 I_0/2 > 0` at
`D_{r_0} Psi_0`; `E:variational-score-set-scaling` (lines 298-304); the set
identity `scoreSet c = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) scoreSet 1` (lines 305-307);
and `BddAbove (scoreSet c)` iff `S1Bdd` for every `c > 0`.
`variational_positive_scores_sSup_paper`, on `S1Bdd`: `S_1^pos > 0` and
`S_c^pos = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) S_1^pos > 0` (first identity of
`E:variational-score-homogeneity`).

Supplied input (named, one): `S1Bdd a Gamma`, `BddAbove (score1Set a Gamma)`,
word for word the boundedness claim of TeX lines 272-274 at `c = 1`, and by
`positive_scores` equivalent to the boundedness for any `c > 0`. Its
manuscript proof (lines 309-325) is stochastic: `T:full-upper` for the same
canonical solution and the point lower bound
`E:variational-unmasked-point-lower` of `P:variational-remove-mask`. Because
`I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are proved genuine first, no junk value enters it; it is
used only by the supremum statements. In wave L8 `S1Bdd` is proved
deterministically under `H:homog` and `Gamma != 0`
(`OccupationCeilingFinite.s1Bdd_paper` over `SpaceTimeCS`, discharged in
`L8Completed.s1Bdd_paper_completed`); the theorems of this module still take
it as a hypothesis, and `L8Completed.variational_positive_scores_sSup_st_paper_completed`
states the supremum part with nothing supplied.

Narrower conclusions (not formalized): the operator half of
`P:variational-unmasked-rate` (self-adjointness of `H_s = -Delta - h_s` on
`H^2`, form domain `H^1`, the spectral bottom `E_s` with `-E_s = sup R_s`,
and so the primary definition `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`; foundation D8); the
second identity `Q_2 >= S_2^pos` of `E:variational-score-homogeneity` (the
stochastic point liminf); the identification `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2`
(`L:compact-raw-profile`). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `I = [0,1]`;
the side condition `integrable_pot` of `WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is
automatic for `h_s`; finiteness is stated as integrability and as bounded
nonempty sets. Hypotheses of `H:homog` used: `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`,
`spectral`, `Gamma_radon`, `scaling`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
`threshold`; the others are carried, unused.

Proof-route differences: the positivity floor uses `h_s >= Gamma * Psibar`
for `s in [0,1]` (`Psibar = int_0^1 Psi(u,.) du`, since
`|s - u|^(-alpha0) >= 1` on `[0,1]^2` off the diagonal `u = s`, which is
Lebesgue-null and excluded almost everywhere in the Lean proof, and Fubini) and the dilation floor
`VariationalFloor.dilation_floor`, not the compact common trial of
`P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines 150-155); `v_Psi > 0` comes from the
positivity of the continuous integrand `Psi(s,x) h_s(x)` at a point, not from
`L:compact-raw-profile`.

## WaveGreen (foundation: the wave Green measures)

Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`) and states
`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lemma, lines 803-848; proof, lines 849-919)
with nothing supplied, except its closing smoothing remark (lines 845-847),
which is formalized in a narrower reading in `DampedMultiplier` and
`WaveGreenFourier` (the spectral identification of the smoothed covariance is
not formalized). Sources of the measures at `a284420`: `d = 1`,
`G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (proof of `L:white-test`, line 746; again at
lines 4128 and 7642); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
5179-5187), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5186-5187). The list of notation
(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 881, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
the supplied input `GreenMass G`.

Definition. `waveGreen d s` is, for `d = 1`, `(1/2)` Lebesgue measure
restricted to the open ball `|x| < s`; for `d = 2`, Lebesgue measure with
density `1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1)` (inside the ball the root
is of a positive number, so no `sqrt` or division junk value enters); for
`d = 3`, `(s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere`; for every other `d`,
the zero measure. For `d = 3` this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4
for wave L6): Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere` (which satisfies
`sigma(A) = 3 vol{r w : 0 < r < 1, w in A}` for measurable `A`, the cone
measure) is taken as the surface measure of the unit sphere, and
`sigma_s = s^2 map (w -> s w) sigma_1` as that of the radius-`s` sphere, so
`sigma_s/(4 pi s) = (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) sigma_1`. Neither
identification with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure is proved.
The manuscript has `d in {1,2,3}` (`H:homog`) and `s >= 0`; the value zero for
other `d` and for `s <= 0` is a Lean convention (`waveGreen_other`,
`waveGreen_of_nonpos`), and every mass and scaling statement carries
`d = 1 \/ d = 2 \/ d = 3`, so no statement holds through it.

Formalized, all proved, nothing supplied: the mass `G_s(R^d) = s` for
`d in {1,2,3}` and every `s >= 0` (`waveGreen_mass`; `s = 0` included, where
the measure is zero); finiteness for every `d` and `s`; support in the closed
radius-`s` ball, `G_s((closedBall 0 s)^c) = 0`, for every `d` and `s`; the
scaling `G_s(sA) = s G_1(A)` for `s > 0` and measurable `A`
(`waveGreen_scaling`; the TeX does not say which sets `A`, and Borel sets are
the reading used; for `d = 1` it holds for every set, `scaling_one`, and
`d = 1` is included although the TeX states the scaling for `d = 2, 3`);
`waveGreen_paper` bundles the four. `waveGreen_greenMass` proves
`GreenMass (waveGreen d)` for `d in {1,2,3}`, so `N0_waveGreen` gives
`N_0(theta) = theta^(-2)` with nothing supplied, and
`damped_homogeneous_norms_wave` states every conclusion of
`DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` with `G := waveGreen d`
under `H:homog` alone (`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal
exponent `a = alpha0`, no `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX; the dimension
condition is `h.dim`). The hypotheses of `H:homog` used are those of
`damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` (listed in the `DampedNormsHomog` section)
plus `dim`, which that section lists as unused but which is used here by
`waveGreen_greenMass d h.dim`; the carried-but-unused fields are that
section's list without `dim`; nothing further is carried. In addition, `waveGreen_fourier_one`
proves for `d = 1` that `int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = G_s hat(xi)` with
`G_s hat = WaveKernel.waveHat` (lines 777-778), with integrability, so the
`d = 1` measure and the multiplier used in `N_1`, `N_2` are linked in Lean;
`WaveGreenFourier` (wave L9) extends the identity to `d = 2, 3`.

Proof route (the TeX quotes masses and scaling from the source, so there is
no TeX proof to follow): `d = 1` by `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball` and
`Gamma(3/2) = sqrt(pi)/2`; `d = 2` by polar coordinates
(`integral_fun_norm_addHaar`) with the antiderivative
`-sqrt(s^2 - r^2)/(2 pi)` of `r (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1)`, and the scaling
by the change of variables `x = s y` (`Measure.map_addHaar_smul`); `d = 3` by
`Measure.toSphere_apply_univ` (total mass `3 vol(B_1) = 4 pi`) and the
preimage identity `{w : s w in sA} = {w : w in A}`; the Fourier identity by
transport to `R` along the coordinate map and
`int_(-s)^s e^(iat) dt = (e^(ias) - e^(-ias))/(ia)` for `a != 0`, and
`= 2s` for `a = 0` (the TeX's value `s` of `G_s hat` at `xi = 0`, lines
777-778). The definitions `radial2`
(the radial density `(2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1)`, with Lean value `0` for
`s^2 <= r^2`, in particular for `0 <= s <= r`, never used there) and `coordOne` (the coordinate `R^1 -> R` as a
measurable equivalence) only name route objects and have no row. Route-only
helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Narrower conclusions: the scaling for measurable `A` only (any set in
`d = 1`); this module proves the Fourier identity in `d = 1`, and
`WaveGreenFourier` (wave L9) proves it in `d = 2, 3` for the same measures
(in `d = 3` for the `toSphere` definition). The identities are not needed for
the conclusions of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` about `N_1`, `N_2`, which are
defined through `waveHat` directly; they identify the second norm of the
Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures with `N_{2,m,S}`
(`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one` in `d = 1`,
`WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave` in `d = 1, 2, 3`).
The lemma with nothing supplied, with its closing smoothing remark in the
narrower reading of the `DampedMultiplier` section (covariance smoothing as
multiplier membership only), is
`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave` (wave L8); the
identification of the smoothed Green norm with `N_{2,m,S}` is not among its
conclusions and is proved separately by the two Fourier wrappers above. The
spectral identification of the smoothed covariance remains unformalized.

## WaveGreenFourier (foundation: Fourier identities of the wave Green measures)

The Fourier identities of the wave Green measures `G_s` in `d = 2, 3`,
Archimedes' law for Mathlib's sphere measure, and the extension of the
Green-smoothing identification of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` to every
`d = 1, 2, 3`, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveGreenFourier.lean`.
Sources (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`):
`G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, value `s` at `xi = 0` (lines
777-778, before `E:damped-norm-definitions`); the display
`G_h hat(xi) = sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, `G_h(R^d) = h` (lines 4740-4744, in
the proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines 4702-4757), which the TeX quotes
from the source's (2.3)-(2.5), p. 7, without proof; the identity is also used
as `G_a hat` in `L:phase-contractions` (lines 2081-2084, 2107-2108, `d = 3`)
and in the proof of `L:alpha-one-convolution` (lines 4760-4818). The measures
are `WaveGreen.waveGreen` (unchanged): in `d = 3` the recorded definitional
choice `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) sigma` with `sigma = volume.toSphere`
(Le's decision 4 for wave L6); this module proves facts about that measure and
does not identify `sigma` with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure.

Formalized, nothing supplied.
- `waveGreen_fourier_two`, `waveGreen_fourier_three`: for `s > 0` and every
  `xi`, `x -> e^(i <xi,x>)` is `G_s`-integrable and
  `int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = waveHat s xi`; `waveGreen_fourier` collects
  `d = 1, 2, 3` (with `WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`), and
  `waveGreen_fourier_paper` states the display at lines 4740-4744 with the
  right side written as in the TeX (`sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, value `h` at
  `0`) together with `G_h(R^d) = h`.
- `sphere_fourier`: `int_(S^2) e^(i <xi,omega>) sigma(d omega) = 4 pi sinc norm(xi)`
  with integrability, the `d = 3` core.
- `archimedes`: for a unit `e`, the image of `sigma` under `omega -> <e,omega>`
  is `2 pi` Lebesgue measure on `[-1,1]`, with the lower-integral,
  integrability and Bochner forms `lintegral_sphere_inner`,
  `integrable_sphere_inner`, `integral_sphere_inner`. It is the image law
  behind "direct integration over its normal coordinate" (lines 2125-2131, used
  in `PhaseContractions`) and "In dimension three spherical coordinates give"
  (lines 5189-5194, proof of `L:higher-riesz`, not formalized).
- `greenFourier`: `DampedMultiplier.GreenFourier (waveGreen d)` for
  `d = 1, 2, 3` (wave L8 proved it in `d = 1` only, `greenFourier_one`).
- `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`: under `H:homog` alone (`d` from the
  field `dim`, no `Gamma != 0`), the conclusions of
  `DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper` with
  `G := waveGreen d`: the second norm of the wave Green measures is
  `N2onSq alpha0 theta S mu` and that of their Gaussian smoothing `p * G`
  (`p = gaussKernel v`, `v >= 0`) is `N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` with
  `m = e^(-v norm(xi)^2)`, with integrability and
  `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2 <= N_{2,1,S'}(theta)^2` (lines 845-847, proof
  915-917). It generalizes `DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`
  to `d = 2, 3`.

Proof route (the TeX has no proof; no Bessel functions). `d = 2`: rotate `xi`
to `norm(xi) e_0` by a reflection (Lebesgue measure is invariant under linear
isometries), slice along `x_0` (Fubini) and use
`int_(-a)^a (a^2 - u^2)^(-1/2) du = pi`. `d = 3`: compute
`int_(norm(x) < R) e^(i <xi,x>) dx` in polar coordinates
(`int_0^R r^2 Phi_xi(r) dr`, `Phi_xi(r) = int e^(i r <xi,omega>) sigma(d omega)`)
and by rotation and slicing (`pi int_(-R)^R (R^2 - t^2) e^(i norm(xi) t) dt`),
and differentiate both in `R` at `R = 1`; no rotation invariance of
`toSphere` is used (Mathlib has none). Archimedes: equality of characteristic
functions (`Measure.ext_of_charFun`). The definitions `splitFirst`
(`R^(n+1) = R x R^n`) and `spherePhi` (`Phi_xi`) only name route objects and
have no row.

Hypotheses. Only `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave` takes `H:homog`; it
uses `dim` directly and passes the hypothesis to
`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper` (fields as recorded
in `DampedMultiplier`). The Fourier identities and Archimedes' law are
statements about the measures alone (`d = 1, 2, 3`, `s > 0`, or `norm(e) = 1`).

Junk values. `WaveGreen.radial2 s r = (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1)` is `0` for
`s^2 <= r^2`, in particular for `0 <= s <= r` (Lean's `sqrt` of a negative number and `0^(-1)` are `0`); it is used
only where it is the density of `waveGreen 2 s` (`waveGreen_two_eq`, `s > 0`)
or inside the slice integral, whose value (`integral_slice_two`) is stated
exactly. Every Fourier conclusion includes the integrability of its integrand.
`Real.sinc 0 = 1` gives the TeX's value `s` at `xi = 0`.

Not formalized here: the spherical computation of lines 5189-5194
(`L:higher-riesz`); `L:alpha-one-convolution`. Narrower conclusions: none for
the identities (the `d = 3` measure is the recorded definitional choice).
Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

## WaveTwoVariances (narrower result: `P:wave-two-variances` for abstract variance and phase spaces, their identification with `ell_R` and the manuscript's spaces not formalized; named inputs; spectral core in full)

Formalizes Proposition `P:wave-two-variances` (Both variance directions) of
`S:wave-variance` (`notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex` at `a284420`:
statement lines 368-383 with `E:wave-input-variance` at lines 374-376 and
`E:wave-output-variance` at lines 377-379, proof lines 385-460 with
`E:variance-kernel-time-bound` at lines 390-393 and
`E:variance-actual-row-bound` at lines 398-401). It also uses the section's
standing assumptions (lines 4-20: `H:homog`, `a = alpha0`,
`E:variance-gamma-range`, `E:variance-scale-profile`), the kernel
`E:variance-normalized-kernel` (lines 229-238), the right side of
`E:variance-normalized-covariance` (lines 240-246), the mask `zeta` and the
interval `I = [t0, t0+h]` (lines 185-188), `C_nu` of
`E:variance-actual-growth-constant` (lines 205-208), the map `J` (lines
171-176) and `E:variance-beta-range` (lines 143-146).

What is formalized. (1) The purely spectral core, with nothing supplied
(`wave_two_variances`, `wave_two_variances_beta`): for any measure `nu` on
`R^d` with `nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha` (open balls, `C >= 0`), any finite
`L^2(R^d; C^2)`-orthonormal family `U_k` (standing for `J e_k`) and any
`V in L^2(R^d; C^2)` (standing for `J z`),
`sum_k int ||int sum_ij 1_I K_ij(.; eta+lambda, eta) U_kj(eta) conj V_i(eta+lambda) d eta||^2_{H_a} nu(d lambda) <= 4 A_T K C h^(2-a) B_alpha(h) ||<xi>^(-gamma) V||_2^2`
(`InputBound`), and, for even `nu`, the same with `U = J z` fixed and an
orthonormal output family `V_k` (`OutputBound`); also with
`4 A_T K_beta C h^(2 beta)` for `beta` in the range of `C:frequency-time`.
`K` is the constant of `P:frequency-row`, `A_T = C1(a)(1+T)^4`. (2) The same
for the manuscript's `nu_R = MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.nu mu zeta R` with the
section's hypotheses (`wave_two_variances_core_paper`,
`wave_two_variances_core_beta_paper`), with `C_T = 4 A_T K C_nu` (line 432),
uniform in `R`, `I` and the family. (3) The proposition itself
(`wave_two_variances_paper`) with three named inputs (below).

Abstractions. `H_a^C` is the concrete completion `TimeCompletion.Ha p` of
`L:masked-time-completion`; `1_I K_ij(.; xi, eta)` is its element `kerH`, the
image of the `L^2(0,T)` class of `maskedKernel` under the continuous
inclusion `TimeCompletion.extL2`; `c_r, b_r` are those of
`L:masked-continuous-wave` (`MaskedContinuousWave.cFn`, `bFn`). The TeX
indices `1, 2` are Lean's `0, 1` (`kernelEntry_matrix` writes out the four
entries). The phases are an abstract complex inner product space `P`
(standing for the Schwartz phases with the complexified `E` inner product),
and `E|l_R(I; z, w)|^2` is an abstract number `var R t0 h z w`.

Supplied inputs (named hypotheses of `wave_two_variances_paper` only; the
core has none). `hlink`: `E:variance-normalized-covariance` (the last claim
of `P:actual-wave-form`, which needs the noise construction D1),
`ofReal(var R t0 h z w) <= int^- ||coef p t0 h (J z) (J w) lambda||^2 nu_R(d lambda)`,
the TeX's display with `U = J z`, `V = J w` (its integral is of a nonnegative
function, lines 410-411); no stronger than its source. `hJL2`, `hJ` (D8):
`J` maps `P` into `L^2(R^d; C^2)` and preserves inner products,
`int sum_j (J z)_j conj((J w)_j) = inner C w z` (Mathlib's `inner C w z` is
linear in `z`, i.e. the TeX's `<z, w>_E`); the TeX's `J` is unitary onto
`L^2(R^d; C^2)`, so this is weaker. `hnormSG` (line 431, D8):
`||z||^2_{E_{s-gamma}} = int <xi>^(-2 gamma) sum_i |(J z)_i|^2`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: the families and `U, V` are `L^2`
componentwise (`MemLp 2`) and orthonormality is
`PhaseBessel.IsOrthonormalL2`; Bochner integrability of every `H_a`-valued
`eta`-integrand is part of the conclusion (so the inner integral is never
Lean's junk `0`); the `lambda` integrals are lower integrals of nonnegative
functions, as in the TeX; the weight integral is a real Bochner integral whose
integrability is part of the conclusion; the general theorems need `gamma >= 0`
(the TeX has `gamma > 0`). In the general form `nu` needs no evenness except
for the output direction, and no local finiteness (it follows from the growth
bound, `isLocallyFinite_of_growth`).

Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): the mask properties of `zeta`
(even, nonnegative, `1` on `B_1`, `0` off `B_2`; growth and evenness of `nu_R`
hold for every real Schwartz `zeta`), `1/2 < beta`, and the fields of
`H:homog` other than `mu_radon` (for s-finiteness), `mu_tempered`, `mu_even`,
`spectral`, `scaling`, `alpha0_lt_one` and `threshold`. `Gamma != 0` is not
assumed: the TeX treats `Gamma = 0` separately (line 202), and here
`nu_R = 0` is covered by the same argument.

Proof route (differences from the TeX). Strong measurability of
`(xi, eta) -> 1_I K_ij(.; xi, eta) in H_a` (lines 404-408) is proved by
continuity (`continuous_kerH`): the entries are jointly continuous in
`((xi, eta), t)` (via `b_r(t) = <r> t sinc(rt)`), hence uniformly continuous
on compact sets, hence continuous into `L^2(0,T)`, and `extL2` is
continuous; no separability argument is used. `E:variance-kernel-time-bound`
is `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted.masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper`
divided by `<xi><eta>` (`norm_kerH_sq_le`), as in the TeX. The fixed-`lambda`
steps (`input_fixed`, `output_fixed`) apply `L:phase-bessel`
(`PhaseBessel.phase_bessel`, `phase_bessel_conj`), the two-component
Cauchy-Schwarz (`sum_norm_sq_le`; its constant `4` is sharp, see the
refutation) and the translation `xi = eta + lambda`. The `lambda`
integration uses lower integrals, superadditivity and Tonelli
(`total_of_fixed`), so measurability of `lambda -> int ... d eta` is not
needed; the row bound `E:variance-actual-row-bound` is the integral clause
of `FrequencyRow.frequency_row`; the output direction reflects `lambda` by
evenness of `nu` and uses `rowKernel_symm`, as at lines 446-450. The
`h^(2 beta)` forms use the time-scale step `FrequencyRow.scale_time_le` of
`C:frequency-time` (the same inequality as the TeX's use of the corollary).
Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve
only this route.

Narrower conclusions. `wave_two_variances_paper` bounds the abstract `var`,
which is tied to `E|l_R|^2` only through `hlink`; `l_R`, the spaces `E_r`
and the unitary `J` are not constructed, and the family is orthonormal in
the abstract `P`. The core results are not narrower than the TeX's proof:
they are lines 385-458 with `nu_R` generalized to any measure with the ball
growth. Not formalized: `P:actual-wave-form` beyond its existing finite
steps (`DimensionalMatrix`), `E:variance-actual-row-bound` as a separate
statement for `nu_R` (it is used inside the core), and
`P:wave-square-columns`.

## WhiteClockLaplace (whole result)

Formalizes `L:white-clock-laplace` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `a284420`, section `S:two-clock-screen`; statement lines 7645-7671, proof
lines 7673-7696) in full, with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing
supplied: the cross-pair transform `E:white-cross-clock-transform` (lines
7648-7659), the diagonal value `K_x(theta,theta) = Gamma(1-a)/(4 theta^(3-a))`
(lines 7660-7661) and the self-pair transform `E:white-self-clock-transform`
(lines 7663-7670), together with the Green-factor steps of the proof. The
section's standing case (lines 7640-7643) is `d = alpha = 1`,
`Gamma = delta_0`, `0 < a < 1` and `G_s(y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (`green`).

The wrapper `white_clock_laplace_paper` assumes `0 < a < 1` (line 7641),
`theta_1, theta_2 > 0` (line 7657) and `eta_1, eta_2 > 0`. The last is an
implicit side condition made explicit: the TeX gives the damping parameters
of the self transform no sign (line 7662, "independent gap damping"), and the
integral converges only for positive `eta`. The integrands are the
definitions `crossIntegrand` and `selfIntegrand` written verbatim, and the
wrapper states their integrability on the open quadrant `(0,inf)^2` and the
values of the iterated integrals in the TeX order (`ds dt` and `dr_1 dr_2`).
The quadrant-integral forms are `cross_transform` and `self_transform`. Every
integral conclusion carries integrability, since a Lean Bochner integral of a
non-integrable function is `0`. At `s = t` Lean's `|s-t|^(-a) = 0^(-a)` is
`0`; the diagonal is a null set, so no stated value depends on it. The Lean
route uses that value only to split the quadrant pointwise
(`crossIntegrand_split`), and this is the only use of `a > 0`. The self
transform needs only `a < 1`, and `a > 0` is carried there for the section's
range. The standing `Gamma = delta_0` and `d = alpha = 1` enter only through
the Green-factor steps. In `green_cross_factor` the `delta_0` pairing
`int int G_s(y) G_t(z) delta_0(y-z) dy dz` is read, as in the TeX, as the
diagonal integral `int G_s(y) G_t(y) dy`; Lean proves the remaining equality
with `min(s,t)/2`. No covariance hypothesis (`H:homog`) is carried, since the
displayed transforms are explicit real integrals.

Proof route: as in the TeX, the quadrant is split into `s = t + v` and
`t = s + v`. In Lean the half `{0 < t < s}` (`upperHalf`) is the image of the
quadrant under the measure-preserving shear `(v,t) -> (v+t,t)`
(`measurePreserving_add_prod`). The half `{0 < s < t}` (`lowerHalf`) reduces
to the first by the coordinate swap, which exchanges `theta_1` and
`theta_2`. Each product integral is computed by `integral_prod_mul`, which is
the Tonelli separation of line 7688. The two elementary integrals of lines
7682-7687 are `laplace_id` and `laplace_rpow`, from Mathlib's
`integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_rpow`. Although grouped in the Lean file
under the Auxiliary heading, their doc comments and statements identify them
as the two TeX proof steps (exactly those displays, with integrability), so
the ledger labels them as proof steps. Every part
of the lemma is formalized. The use of these transforms in the rest of
`S:two-clock-screen` is outside this module.

## WhiteRelativeWidth (whole result)

Formalizes `C:white-relative-width` (`notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex`
at `a284420`, statement lines 130-138, proof lines 140-161) in full, with the
manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied. The two formulas it compares are
those displayed in `T:white-moment-bounds` (`E:white-moment-bounds`, lines
101-111): `K_0(a) = 2^a/(1-a)` (`boundK0`) and
`M_a = Gamma((1+a)/2)/(Gamma(1+a) Gamma((1-a)/2))` (`boundMass`), with the
lower formula `(2/3) sqrt(c/M_a)` (`lowerFormula`) and the upper formula
`(2/3) sqrt(c K_0(a))` (`upperFormula`). These four are definitions of real
expressions only. Lean proves the identities and the inequality between the
displayed formulas: that the intrinsic constant `C_2(c,a)` lies between the
lower and upper formulas is `T:white-moment-bounds`, which is outside Lean and
is neither used nor proved here. Nothing of `P:white-spatial-energy` (the CDF
square identity, `H^1` profiles, the spatial energy constant; reserved package
B9) is used or proved.

The wrapper `white_relative_width_paper` assumes exactly `c > 0` (line 132) and
the section's `0 < a < 1` (line 5). It concludes that the ratio of the upper to
the lower formula is `sqrt(K_0(a) M_a)`, that this is at most
`[sqrt(pi)/(2 Gamma(5/4)^2)]^(1/2)`, and that equality holds if `a = 1/2`.
`Gamma_E` is Mathlib's `Real.Gamma`, `2^a` is `Real.rpow`, and the square
roots, including `[.]^(1/2)`, are `Real.sqrt`. Every quantity under a square
root or in a denominator is shown positive for `0 < a < 1` (`boundK0_pos`,
`boundMass_pos`), so no statement relies on Lean's `sqrt` of a negative number
or `x/0 = 0`. All hypotheses are used. Also proved: the closing remark of the
proof that this ratio is symmetric under `a -> 1-a` (lines 158-159), and
`boundMass_eq_mass`, which identifies the displayed `M_a` with
`TemporalEquilibrium.mass a`, the mass of `L:temporal-equilibrium`
(`E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`), for `0 < a < 1`. That identification is not
stated in the corollary.

Proof route: the duplication and recurrence steps (lines 141-147) are those of
the TeX, taken from `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta`
(`TemporalEquilibrium.gamma_beta_duplication_general`,
`gamma_beta_recurrence`). The inequality
`Gamma(5/4)^2 <= Gamma(1+a/2) Gamma((3-a)/2)` (with `x + y = 5/2`) is proved
from the log-convexity of `Gamma` on `(0, inf)` (Mathlib's
`Real.convexOn_log_Gamma`, through the auxiliary `gamma_mid_sq_le`), not by
Cauchy-Schwarz in Euler's integral as in the TeX (lines 153-157); the
inequality is the same. Every part of the corollary is formalized; the
surrounding `T:white-moment-bounds` and `P:white-spatial-energy` stay outside.

## Not in Lean

The main analytic ingredients of the manuscript are not formalized here.
In particular:

- Existence of the canonical solution and its expansion, including
  self-pairings and fixed-order coefficients (`P:mild-construction`, of whose
  proof only the finite-coordinate multiplication bound
  `E:occupied-multiplication` is in `FockForm`; `L:joint-fixed-order`), and
  the crude bound `T:crude`.
- The upper bound at the scale `t^kappa` (`T:full-upper`) and the spectral
  and operator estimates behind it: the spatial half of `L:fock-form` and
  `E:interval-column`, supplied to `FockForm` as `FockColumn`; the phase
  propagator of `L:complex-phase` and `L:interval-complex`, Crouzeix-Palencia
  `E:cp-input`, the inverse-root integral representation and the
  identification of the propagator with the weighted block map (their
  scalar, numerical-range and Banach-algebra steps are in
  `ComplexPhaseScalar`), the telescoping of `E:interval-metric` along a time

  `FockForm`; `L:finite-word-cutoff` is in `HermiteWordFock` for one Gaussian

- Equality in law under the exact scaling (`L:exact-canonical-scaling`),
